The Serve fleet has been delighting merchants, customers, and pedestrians along the way in Los Angeles, Miami, Dallas, Atlanta and Chicago while doing commercial deliveries. We’re looking for talented individuals who will grow robotic deliveries from surprising novelty to efficient ubiquity.

Who We Are

We are tech industry veterans in software, hardware, and design who are pooling our skills to build the future we want to live in. We are solving real-world problems leveraging robotics, machine learning and computer vision, among other disciplines, with a mindful eye towards the end-to-end user experience. Our team is agile, diverse, and driven. We believe that the best way to solve complicated dynamic problems is collaboratively and respectfully.

Responsibilities

  • Design, develop, test, and maintain robotics middleware and application frameworks using modern C++ on embedded Linux.

  • Own significant platform components from technical design and implementation through validation, deployment, and operation across Serve’s robot fleet.

  • Partner with software teams using the robot platform to identify reliability, performance, and developer experience problems and deliver reusable solutions.

  • Collaborate with Autonomy and Systems Engineering on risk assessments, failure analysis, fault-handling strategies, and software architecture.

  • Translate system-level safety and reliability requirements into software behavior, interfaces, and verification strategies.

  • Develop instrumentation, benchmarks, logging, tracing, and fleet-level metrics to measure and improve software performance, reliability, and system health.

  • Diagnose and resolve complex system-level issues involving concurrency, scheduling, interprocess communication, networking, and constrained compute resources.

  • Evaluate technical tradeoffs and contribute to architectural decisions that improve the scalability, maintainability, and reliability of the robotics platform.

  • Lead technical design and code reviews and contribute to engineering standards, development practices, and technical documentation.

  • Provide technical guidance and mentorship to other engineers through design discussions, problem solving, and knowledge sharing.

Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Robotics, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a related technical discipline, or equivalent practical experience.

  • 5+ years of professional software engineering experience, including significant experience developing production software in modern C++ (C++17 and newer).

  • Experience developing and debugging systems software in embedded Linux environments.

  • Strong understanding of multithreaded programming, concurrency, synchronization, interprocess communication, and systems-level software development.

  • Experience designing software for latency-sensitive, safety-related, real-time, or high-reliability systems.

  • Experience profiling and optimizing embedded software for performance, reliability, and resource utilization.

  • Experience independently owning complex software components through design, implementation, testing, and deployment.

  • Strong troubleshooting and problem-solving skills with demonstrated ability to diagnose complex issues across software and hardware boundaries.

  • Strong written and verbal communication skills and the ability to collaborate effectively across software, systems, and hardware engineering teams.

What Makes You Stand Out

  • Experience developing middleware for robotics, autonomous vehicles, or similar complex systems.

  • Experience developing and deploying production software on NVIDIA Jetson or similar embedded computing platforms.

  • Knowledge of Linux internals, scheduling, resource management, device interfaces, and interprocess communication mechanisms.

  • Experience with fault-tolerant architecture, failure-mode analysis, functional safety, or safety-related software development.

  • Experience with distributed systems, networking, RPC frameworks, or serialization technologies such as Protocol Buffers, FlatBuffers, or Cap’n Proto.

  • Experience developing telemetry, observability, health monitoring, or diagnostic capabilities for robotics or distributed device fleets.

  • Experience integrating software with sensors, embedded hardware, or other robotic system components.

Additional Information:

This role works across multiple engineering disciplines and balances hands-on software development with systems-level problem solving, technical design, and cross-functional collaboration. The position may occasionally require access to robotics hardware or onsite participation in integration, testing, troubleshooting, or validation activities.

Who We Are

At RelationalAI, we’re solving one of the most important challenges in artificial intelligence: how to teach large language models the logic, semantics, and business context of the modern enterprise.

Frontier models are trained almost entirely on public data — they can speak about the world, but they don’t understand your business. We fix that.

RelationalAI has pioneered a breakthrough called Superalignment — technology that enables LLMs to learn natively from private, structured enterprise data inside the data cloud.

By combining this with relational knowledge graphs and our proprietary neuro/symbolic-relational reasoners, we deliver trustworthy decision intelligence: systems that use semantic models to truly understand how a business operates and can reason across its data to drive better outcomes.

We’re a globally distributed team of engineers, scientists, and builders redefining how AI learns from data. We believe that high-stakes decisions deserve frontier intelligence — intelligence that’s explainable, aligned, and grounded in reality.

If you’re driven by curiosity, thrive in complexity, and want to help build the system that brings true understanding to enterprise AI, you’ll feel right at home here.

The Role

You will be embedded inside our customers' hardest problems, and you will own the outcome until it works in production.

You'll sit with executives, domain experts, and data teams to find the decisions that actually move their business - inventory that's in the wrong place, risk concentrations nobody can see, fraud patterns that only emerge across three systems, capacity plans built on guesses. Then you'll model their world in our ontology, formulate the reasoning problem, write the PyRel, and ship something that runs against their real data in their own Snowflake account.

Every engagement here produces two deliverables.

The first is the one the customer sees: a working decision system that changes how they operate.

The second is the one that matters most to us: the pile of things you had to invent because our platform didn't have them yet. The modelling pattern you hand-rolled. The constraint formulation that should have been a primitive. The three-hour workaround where an API should have existed. You bring those back, you argue for them, and the strongest of them become product.

That second deliverable is why this role exists. If you only ever deliver the first one, we've hired a consultant. We're not hiring consultants.

You'll operate with unusual autonomy: you decide what's worth building, when a workaround is acceptable and when it's technical debt we'll regret, and when to tell a customer their real problem is not the one they asked about. You'll be technical enough that when something breaks in a customer environment, you find the root cause yourself rather than filing a ticket and waiting.

What You'll Do

  • Own outcomes end to end - discovery, modelling, implementation, performance tuning, production hardening, and the measurement that proves it worked. Not a handoff at each stage. Yours.
  • Build, not describe - design and ship decision solutions on our modelling, reasoning, and learning stack: ontologies over customer data, rules, graph analytics, optimisation formulations, predictive models
  • Fill the gaps yourself - when a customer workflow is blocked on something the platform doesn't do, scope it and build it. Then push the general version upstream: read our source, form a hypothesis before you escalate, open the PR.
  • Close the loop with Product - every deployment generates a signal. Bring back reproductions, patterns, and specific failure modes ("the only way I could express this was by abusing X in this way"), not vibes. You are one of the loudest inputs into our roadmap.
  • Run technical discovery that gets to the truth - workshops, demos, and proofs of concept designed to find out whether we can actually solve the problem, not to look impressive.
  • Leave things better than you found them - document as you go, in the repo, same week. Turn one-off work into reusable reference implementations so the next person starts where you finished. No branch of yours should be diverging for a month.
  • Refuse shortcuts that compound - no undocumented config drift, no "it works now" without knowing why it broke, no restarting the service before you've captured the evidence.

Who You Are

You thrive in ambiguity and move with intent. You're motivated by deep understanding and meaningful impact.

  • Owner, not participant. You take full accountability for the outcome, not your slice of it. When something is broken and it's nobody's job, it becomes yours.
  • You build. Your instinct in the face of a hard problem is to open an editor, not a deck. You'd rather show a working prototype on real data than a diagram of one.
  • High conviction, low ego. You argue hard for what you believe, you're direct about what's wrong, and you change your mind quickly when the evidence turns. You challenge ideas without making it personal - people leave arguments with you feeling sharper, not smaller.
  • Rigorous. You root-cause things. You can explain both why it broke and why your fix works. Surface symptoms don't satisfy you.
  • Fast in unfamiliar territory. Dropped into a codebase, a domain, or a data model you've never seen, you're useful within days. "I only do backend" and "that's not my job" are phrases you don't use.
  • High tolerance for friction. Enterprise environments are messy - broken data, VDI access, security reviews, politics. You route around it and keep shipping.
  • Impact-driven. You want the thing you built to still be running, and still be load-bearing, two years from now.

What This Role Is Not

We'd rather be blunt than waste your time:

  • It is not demo-and-handoff pre-sales. You don't disappear after the POC; you're there when it goes to production.
  • It is not staff augmentation. You own outcomes, not hours or ticket queues.
  • It is not advisory. We deliver working software, not recommendations.
  • It is not a support role. You deploy new things; you don't maintain someone else's legacy.

Qualifications

  • 5+ years building and shipping production software, at least some of it inside customer or partner environments
  • Demonstrated end-to-end ownership: you have personally taken something from an ambiguous problem statement to running in production, and you can walk us through the whole arc, including what went wrong
  • Strong SQL and deep familiarity with cloud data platforms (Snowflake, BigQuery, Databricks, Redshift)
  • Strong programming ability - Python primarily; comfort with declarative or logic-style languages is a real advantage
  • Comfortable reading unfamiliar source code, interpreting stack traces, and debugging systems you didn't write
  • Able to hold your own with both a VP of Supply Chain and a staff data engineer, in the same meeting
  • Comfortable operating in high-autonomy, high-velocity, low-instruction environments

Preferred Qualifications

  • Built analytical, decision, or reasoning applications that reached production and stayed there
  • Experience with optimization, constraint solving, rule engines, graph algorithms, or ML on structured data
  • Semantic modelling, data pipelines, and governance in real enterprise settings
  • Track record of upstream contribution - features, tools, or abstractions you built for one customer that became standard for everyone
  • Prior experience in enterprise technology, AI, or analytics platforms

How We Hire

Our loop is designed to test the job, not trivia. Expect a technical screen; a session where you navigate and extend a system you've never seen before; a problem-decomposition session on a realistic customer scenario; and a conversation about ownership with the hiring manager. We're looking for how you think when you don't know the answer.

The Solution Engineer position offers a base salary range of $170,000 to $200,000, along with equity and comprehensive benefits. Please note that this range serves as a guideline; actual total compensation may vary based on factors such as experience, skill set, qualifications, and geographic location.

Why RelationalAI

At RelationalAI, you will:

  • Work from anywhere in the world
  • Earn competitive salary + equity
  • Enjoy open PTO, flexible schedules, and recharge weeks
  • Access global benefits, mental-health support, and learning stipends
  • Join a transparent, inclusive, and globally connected culture that values curiosity, excellence, and impact
  • Regular team offsites and global events – Building strong connections while working remotely through team offsites and global events that bring everyone together.
  • A culture of transparency & knowledge-sharing – Open communication through team standups, fireside chats, and open meetings.

Country Hiring Guidelines:

RelationalAI hires people from around the world. All of our roles are remote; however, some locations might carry specific eligibility requirements.

Because of this, understanding location & visa support helps us better prepare to onboard our colleagues.

Our People Operations team can help answer any questions about location after starting the recruitment process.

How to Apply

If you’re driven by understanding, powered by curiosity, and ready to help shape the next era of enterprise intelligence — we’d love to hear from you.

Join us and help build the reasoning layer for the modern enterprise.

As Head of Product, you own our product hands-on. You are the bridge between what the market and our operators need and what we build, turning field feedback and market insight into a clear roadmap and products people actually want to use. You own how our capabilities become real products: how they are shaped, packaged, priced, taken to market, and adopted by the people who use them in the field.

This is a hands-on, roll-up-your-sleeves role, not a purely strategic one. • Market-to-technical bridge. Translating operator needs, market signals, and partner requirements into clear, well-scoped work for engineering, and translating technical capability back into value the market understands.

• A working feedback loop that turns field and operational insight into product decisions.

• Well-scoped, prioritized work flowing to engineering, with product shipped and validated with users.

• A joint go-to-market plan with commercial for at least one capability, taken through to execution.

• Measurable improvement in product adoption and usability through better onboarding, documentation, and training for operators and partners.

• A working market map that informs the next set of product bets.

• 5+ years in product management, with a track record of owning a product’s roadmap and shipping it in a technical product environment.

• Experience in a startup or scale-up environment: comfortable with ambiguity, limited resources, and wearing several hats.

• A strong bridge-builder: you connect customers and market reality to engineering, and you are comfortable in deeply technical conversations without being the engineer yourself.

• A genuinely hands-on mindset: you want to talk to users, write requirements, and work day-to-day with engineering, not only set direction from a distance.

• Exposure to pricing, packaging, and business-model decisions (the product side of the 4Ps).

• Experience working with commercial teams on go-to-market.

• A user-obsessed attitude: you care about adoption, usability, training, and documentation, not only features.

• The ability to read a market, spot trends, and turn them into concrete product opportunities.

• Strong communication and stakeholder skills, from the field and the shop floor to founders, partners, and government stakeholders.

• Domain experience in defence, drones/UAV, aerospace, or other dual-use or high-stakes technology. A real plus, but not a must.

• Experience navigating regulated environments and their impact on product, such as export control, procurement, certification, or standards.

  • Prepare environments, transports and go-lives, and hand over to the support team

3. SAP Analytics Expert – Evolutive Maintenance & New Developments (mini-projects) | approx. 45%

  • Define the target analytics architecture (BW/IP, HANA, CDS, BO/Lumira, SLT) in line with the SAP roadmap and cloud analytics solutions

  • Lead scoping and GAP analysis, and deliver documented recommendations backed by SAP references and SWOT analysis

  • Lead POCs and validate performance and reporting output

  • Conduct design reviews, performance analysis and optimisation

Your Profile (all positions):

  • Senior-level SAP Analytics / BI experience on S/4HANA (for the Expert position: expert level, with proven experience in leading analytics architecture and design)

  • Strong BW / BW-IP skills in design, modelling, data loading, financial reporting and budget planning

  • Hands-on experience with financial reporting tools: AfO, BEx Analyzer, BEx Query Designer, WAD and broadcasting

  • Experience in budget planning, including planning models, simulations, consolidation and reporting

  • Solid knowledge of SAP BusinessObjects, Lumira and migration to WebI (N4V for WebI is a plus)

  • Experience designing, extending and optimising CDS Views and HANA Views

  • ABAP skills to maintain and enhance a custom program generating XML for output management

  • Understanding of integration across CRM, S/4HANA, BW, HANA and reporting tools, with a focus on data quality, performance, security and governance

  • Knowledge of management accounting (controlling) and project management

  • Familiarity with RUN processes: incident resolution, SPS/SP cycles, regression testing, transports and Basis validation

  • Experience with Jira, ChaRM, Solution Manager and Confluence

  • Knowledge of SAP cloud analytics solutions (and, for the Expert position, the SAP analytics roadmap)

  • SAP Analytics certifications (BW, BW-IP, CDS Views, SLT, BO, Lumira, SAP cloud analytics) are an advantage

  • Fluent French is essential

What We Offer:

  • A long-term engagement through 2029, renewable annually

  • Meaningful work supporting the financial and budget processes of a public-sector organisation

  • A broad and modern SAP Analytics landscape covering BW/IP, HANA, CDS, SLT, BO/Lumira and cloud analytics

  • A choice of focus (RUN, BUILD or architecture) to suit your expertise and availability

  • Collaboration within an experienced internal SAP Finance / Analytics team

  • Remote working after the onboarding phase

  • Opportunities to shape the client’s analytics architecture and future roadmap

description: We are currently looking for an experienced Senior IT & Cybersecurity Auditor to join an international financial services environment and contribute to strengthening its technology, cybersecurity and risk management landscape. In this role, you will combine your technical expertise with a strong understanding of governance, risk and controls. You will take ownership of complex audit engagements, challenge existing practices and provide independent insights that support informed decision-making at senior management level. This is an excellent opportunity for a technically experienced professional who enjoys investigating complex IT environments, identifying potential vulnerabilities and making a meaningful impact on the organisation’s security and resilience. Responsibilities & Tasks Plan, lead and deliver comprehensive IT audit engagements based on a risk-oriented approach, including the development of audit strategies and testing procedures. Review and evaluate technology-related risk areas, including cybersecurity, IT governance, infrastructure, network security, access management, data protection, operational resilience and emerging technologies. Apply your technical background to analyse complex IT architectures, identify potential weaknesses and assess the effectiveness of existing security measures and internal controls. Review findings from penetration tests, vulnerability scans, security assessments and monitoring activities, translating technical observations into relevant risk insights. Assess emerging technologies, particularly Artificial Intelligence and AI-driven solutions, and evaluate their implications for cybersecurity, governance and technology risk. Present audit findings, recommendations and risk assessments to relevant stakeholders, including senior management and executive-level decision-makers. Prepare structured and impactful audit documentation, ensuring that identified issues are clearly communicated and actionable. Track remediation activities and evaluate the effectiveness of implemented measures. Work closely with colleagues across IT, Cybersecurity, Risk Management, Governance and Business functions to promote continuous improvement and strengthen the overall control environment. Requirements & Qualifications Degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Information Systems or a comparable discipline, alternatively equivalent professional experience. At least 10 years of relevant professional experience in IT, Cybersecurity, Information Security, Technology Risk or a related technical field. Strong practical knowledge of several core technology and security domains, such as Network Security, Identity and Access Management, Vulnerability Management, Security Operations or IT Resilience. Experience working with technical security assessments, penetration testing results, vulnerability scanning solutions or comparable security tools. Previous exposure to IT Audit, Internal Audit, External Audit, Technology Risk or another assurance-related function is highly desirable. Professional certifications such as CISA, CISM, CISSP or equivalent qualifications are considered an advantage. Interest in Artificial Intelligence, machine learning and AI-driven technologies, particularly in relation to security, governance and risk management. Practical experience in AI governance or AI-based solutions is beneficial. Strong analytical capabilities, a structured approach to problem-solving and the ability to assess complex technical information independently. Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills, with the confidence to challenge established practices constructively and engage with senior decision-makers. High professional integrity, sound judgement and a strong sense of responsibility. Fluent English is required. German and/or French language skills are an additional advantage. Willingness to undertake international business travel, approximately 20 days or more annually. Benefits & Culture Work in an international financial services environment where technology, security and risk management play a central role. Take on a highly visible position with direct exposure to senior stakeholders and strategic decision-making. Enjoy a broad and varied scope of responsibility across technology, cybersecurity and emerging risk areas. Collaborate with experienced professionals from IT, Business, Risk and Governance in a supportive and knowledge-driven environment. Benefit from opportunities for continuous professional development, specialist training and relevant industry certifications. Contribute to meaningful initiatives that strengthen organisational security, resilience and governance. title: Staff Software Engineer - OpenTelemetry Python instrumentation | UK | Remote
description: Grafana Labs is the company behind Grafana Cloud, the fully managed observability platform trusted by more than 10,000 organizations to ensure reliability, resolve incidents faster, and optimize telemetry at scale. Built on open source and open standards and designed for interoperability across any stack, Grafana Cloud brings AI to observability and observability to AI, giving teams (and their agents) unified visibility so they can see, understand, and act on all their disparate data, wherever it lives, and move at the speed of their ambitions. Customers, including Anthropic, Bloomberg, NVIDIA, Microsoft, and Salesforce, rely on Grafana Labs. We are a 100% remote company with team members across 40+ countries, backed by leading investors including Lightspeed Venture Partners, Sequoia Capital, GIC, Coatue, J.P. Morgan, CapitalG, and Lead Edge Capital. Learn more at grafana.com and follow us on LinkedIn and X . We’re scaling fast and staying true to what makes us different: an open-source legacy, a global collaborative culture, and a passion for meaningful work. Our team thrives in an innovation-driven environment where transparency, autonomy, and trust fuel everything we do. You may not meet every requirement, and that’s okay. If this role excites you, we’d love you to raise your hand for what could be a truly career-defining opportunity. This is a remote opportunity and we would be interested in applications from Germany, UK, Ireland and Spain. The Opportunity: Grafana Cloud is our composable observability platform that integrates metrics, logs, and traces with Grafana. It allows our customers to leverage the best open source observability software – including Prometheus, Mimir, Loki, and Tempo – without the overhead of installing, maintaining and scaling their own observability stack The Observability department is focused on enabling developers to understand the health and performance of their applications and infrastructure in any environment by providing tools to instrument their code, ingest observability data into Grafana Cloud and visualize and explore it. The OpenTelemetry SDKs team's mission is to make sure our users succeed in instrumenting their software with OpenTelemetry. We work closely with the OpenTelemetry SIGs to make OpenTelemetry SDKs and instrumentation libraries a success. Members of this team are experts in at least one programming language and have a broad knowledge of various other programming languages. In this role, you will focus on a language-specific implementation of OpenTelemetry in Python , with an emphasis on OpenTelemetry for Generative AI . You will get to work in an upstream-first approach, helping accelerate the OpenTelemetry project while bringing the innovations to Grafana labs products and offerings. As a company we are remote-first and global, we embrace people of different experiences and backgrounds to build diverse teams where every person brings a unique perspective to the software. We are looking for Engineers that are passionate about communicating with data and providing seamless experiences for our customers to join our growing team! Engineers at Grafana also have the opportunity to contribute to Open Source communities. At Grafana Labs, ICs have a dedicated career path and do not have to become managers to progress in their career. Staff Software Engineers at Grafana have a large amount of experience across multiple areas. They are able to estimate, plan, coordinate and deliver large tasks spanning multiple systems. They actively coach and mentor other team members in their team and are able to identify and resolve issues with technology and product processes. What You’ll Be Doing: You will bring your software engineering expertise to develop improvements to the OpenTelemetry Python SDK and instrumentation libraries, with a strong focus on AI applications and agent workflows. This is a hands-on role for someone with deep Python expertise and an interest in AI. Collaborate in open-source communities. You will develop and maintain the OpenTelemetry Python SDK and instrumentation libraries, working with maintainers and other vendors on specifications, APIs, and implementation decisions. Build Python instrumentation for AI agents. Build instrumentation that connects agent runs, model calls, and tool execution, including across asynchronous code. Contribute to evolving OpenTelemetry conventions for generative AI, with care for sensitive data and metric cardinality. Improve Python SDK performance. Use profiling and benchmarks to evaluate implementation approaches with the upstream community. Make sound tradeoffs around runtime overhead, compatibility, and maintainability. Be visible as an OpenTelemetry expert. Teach others, promote best practices around OpenTelemetry, semantic conventions, and various technologies and frameworks. Both within Grafana Labs and in the broader OpenTelemetry community. Support the technical direction and vision of the team, and contribute to business conversations on the OpenTelemetry strategy at Grafana Labs. Own projects from an ambiguous problem through design, implementation, testing, documentation, and release. Partner in an open and respectful way. Lend your knowledge and skills to our GTM, Product and Support teams. Join customer conversations, investigate instrumentation issues, and turn what you learn into fixes and practical guidance. As we are remote-first and our engineering organization is largely remote, we provide guidance and meet regularly using video calls, so high agency and good communication skills are a must. What Makes You a Great Fit: At Grafana Labs, Staff Engineers are defined by the impact they have and the people they enable. You take ownership of complex problems, set technical direction, and help others deliver improvements that matter to customers and the OpenTelemetry community. 8+ years of experience in software development, with strong proficiency in Python and experience debugging production software, language internals, libraries, and asynchronous code. An interest in AI applications and agent systems, and curiosity about how to instrument and troubleshoot them. Prior experience building AI systems is helpful, but not required. Experience working in open-source communities. You are eager to become an active member of the OpenTelemetry community, collaborate with maintainers and users, and keep learning across languages, frameworks, and the wider observability ecosystem. Familiarity with observability tooling such as Grafana, Prometheus, and OpenTelemetry, alongside experience with cloud-based software or systems engineering. You understand production environments and can assess operational risks. Bonus Points For: You have experience working on open source observability projects, ideally in OpenTelemetry or Prometheus. Experience in Python instrumentation techniques, profiling, runtime diagnostics, or asynchronous context propagation Experience in a hands-on technical leadership role, setting technical direction and leading project teams Experience instrumenting AI frameworks or agent workflows, or working with OpenTelemetry semantic conventions for generative AI Experience contributing to or maintaining Open Source projects, with evidence of successful pull requests and community collaboration Rust experience is a plus for exploring potential Python SDK performance improvements, including Rust-backed implementations. Compensation & Rewards: In the UK, the compensation range for this role is GBP 107,000 - GBP 134,000. Actual compensation may vary based on level, experience, and skillset as assessed throughout the interview process. All of our roles include Restricted Stock Units (RSUs), giving every team member ownership in Grafana Labs' success. We believe in shared outcomes—RSUs help us stay aligned and invested as we scale globally. *Compensation ranges are country specific. If you are applying for this role from a different location than listed above, your recruiter will discuss your specific market’s defined pay range & benefits at the beginning of the process. Why You’ll Thrive at Grafana Labs: 100% Remote, Global Culture - As a remote-only company, we bring together talent from around the world, united by a culture of collaboration and shared purpose. Scaling Organization – Tackle meaningful work in a high-growth, ever-evolving environment. Transparent Communication – Expect open decision-making and regular company-wide updates. Innovation-Driven – Autonomy and support to ship great work and try new things. Open Source Roots – Built on community-driven values that shape how we work. Empowered Teams – High trust, low ego culture that values outcomes over optics. Career Growth Pathways – Defined opportunities to grow and develop your career. Approachable Leadership – Transparent execs who are involved, visible, and human. Passionate People – Join a team of smart, supportive folks who care deeply about what they do. In-Person onboarding - We want you to thrive from day 1 with your fellow new ‘Grafanistas’ to learn all about what we do and how we do it. Balance is Key - We operate a global annual leave policy of 30 days per annum. 3 days of your annual leave entitlement are reserved for Grafana Shutdown Days to allow the team to really disconnect. *We will comply with local legislation where applicable. Equal Opportunity Employer: Grafana Labs is an equal opportunities employer. We welcome applications from everyone regardless of race, colour, nationality, origin, caste, sex, gender reassignment identity or expression, sexual orientation, age, religion or belief, disability, veteran status, genetic information, pregnancy, maternity, marital, family or carer status, or any other characteristic which is protected by local law. We believe that equality and diversity build a strong organisation, and we work hard to ensure that is the foundation of our organisation as we grow. Grafana Labs may utilize AI tools in its recruitment process to assist in matching information provided in CVs to job postings. The recruitment team will continue to review inbound CVs manually to identify alignment with current openings. #LI-Remote For information about how your personal data is used once you’ve applied to a job, check out our privacy policy .

As a company we are remote-first and global, we embrace people of different experiences and backgrounds to build diverse teams where every person brings a unique perspective to the software. We are looking for Engineers that are passionate about communicating with data and providing seamless experiences for our customers to join our growing team! You will bring your software engineering expertise to develop improvements to the OpenTelemetry Python SDK and instrumentation libraries, with a strong focus on AI applications and agent workflows. This is a hands-on role for someone with deep Python expertise and an interest in AI.

  • Collaborate in open-source communities. You will develop and maintain the OpenTelemetry Python SDK and instrumentation libraries, working with maintainers and other vendors on specifications, APIs, and implementation decisions.
  • Build Python instrumentation for AI agents. Build instrumentation that connects agent runs, model calls, and tool execution, including across asynchronous code. Contribute to evolving OpenTelemetry conventions for generative AI, with care for sensitive data and metric cardinality.
  • Improve Python SDK performance. Use profiling and benchmarks to evaluate implementation approaches with the upstream community. Make sound tradeoffs around runtime overhead, compatibility, and maintainability.
  • Be visible as an OpenTelemetry expert. Teach others, promote best practices around OpenTelemetry, semantic conventions, and various technologies and frameworks. Both within Grafana Labs and in the broader OpenTelemetry community.
  • Support the technical direction and vision of the team, and contribute to business conversations on the OpenTelemetry strategy at Grafana Labs. Own projects from an ambiguous problem through design, implementation, testing, documentation, and release.
  • Partner in an open and respectful way. Lend your knowledge and skills to our GTM, Product and Support teams. Join customer conversations, investigate instrumentation issues, and turn what you learn into fixes and practical guidance.

As we are remote-first and our engineering organization is largely remote, we provide guidance and meet regularly using video calls, so high agency and good communication skills are a must.

At Grafana Labs, Staff Engineers are defined by the impact they have and the people they enable. You take ownership of complex problems, set technical direction, and help others deliver improvements that matter to customers and the OpenTelemetry community.

  • An interest in AI applications and agent systems, and curiosity about how to instrument and troubleshoot them. Prior experience building AI systems is helpful, but not required.

  • Rust experience is a plus for exploring potential Python SDK performance improvements, including Rust-backed implementations.

raw.jobDescription:
About Nebius:

Nebius is leading a new era in cloud infrastructure for the global AI economy. We are building a full-stack AI cloud platform that supports developers and enterprises from data and model training through to production deployment, without the cost and complexity of building large in-house AI/ML infrastructure.

Built by engineers, for engineers. From large-scale GPU orchestration to inference optimization, we own the hard problems across compute, storage, networking and applied AI.

Listed on Nasdaq (NBIS) and headquartered in Amsterdam, we have a global footprint with R&D hubs across Europe, the UK, North America and Israel. Our team of 1,500+ includes hundreds of engineers with deep expertise across hardware, software and AI R&D.

The Role

We’re looking for a Software Engineer to build software that makes network operations safe, scalable, and boring — even as we launch new data centers and expand fast. This is not a “write scripts for configs” role: you’ll build the tooling and services that sit between the network core (switches/ports/VLANs, traffic processors) and the cloud platform on top, using open source where it fits and building the missing pieces where it doesn’t.

Your responsibilities will include:

  • Build and maintain services and tooling that automate the network lifecycle: day-0 provisioning, day-N changes, drift detection, and operational verification
  • Make network changes safe and transparent: CI/CD workflows, diff/review tooling, staged rollouts/rollbacks, audit trails, and guardrails
  • Develop observability systems that scale across many sites: telemetry pipelines, signal quality, and tooling that shortens incident investigations
  • Close “last mile” gaps between the network and the platform: integrate source-of-truth data, expose APIs, and build reliable automation around it
  • Collaborate closely with network engineers and SREs to turn real operational pain into product-quality tooling

We expect you to have:

  • 5+ years of professional software engineering experience (or equivalent practical background)
  • Strong coding skills and ownership mindset: you can ship and operate reliable services
  • Proficiency in Go or readiness to switch; Python is also welcome (other languages can be useful for OSS debugging/fixes)
  • You don’t have to be Network expert but we expect you to have interest in infrastructure and/or network

It will be an added bonus if you have:

  • Background in networking (ex-network engineer, CCNP/education, DC networking exposure) or strong interest and proven ability to learn fast
  • Experience building automation/infra tooling: CI/CD, IaC, testing/staging environments, or “network-as-code” style workflows
  • Low-level networking / datapath experience: eBPF/XDP, DPDK, kernel networking, traffic processing systems
  • Experience designing high-load services and observability platforms (metrics/logs/traces, alerting, regression detection)
  • Contributions to open source or experience extending/debugging OSS components in production environments

We expect Engineers to:

  • Manage large-scale projects involving multiple stakeholders
  • Break down complex tasks and guide both their own work and that of more junior colleagues
  • Be experts in specific technologies and write high-quality code that can serve as a reference
  • Assess task priority and focus on high-impact work, avoiding low-value efforts
  • Have strong architectural thinking and contribute to system design
  • Be involved in hiring and actively contribute to interviews
  • Be willing to share knowledge and mentor others

Benefits & Perks:

  • Competitive compensation
  • Career growth and learning opportunities
  • Flexibility and ownership
  • Collaborative and innovative culture
  • Opportunity to work on impactful AI projects
  • International environment and talented teams

What's it like to work at Nebius:

Fast moving - Bold thinking - Constant growth - Meaningful impact - Trust and real ownership - Opportunity to shape the future of AI

Equal Opportunity Statement:

Nebius is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to fostering an inclusive and diverse workplace and to providing equal employment opportunities in all aspects of employment. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex (including pregnancy), national origin, ancestry, age, disability, genetic information, marital status, veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

Applicants must be authorized to work in the country in which they apply and will be required to provide proof of employment eligibility as a condition of hire.

If you need accommodations during the application process, please let us know.

title: GTM Engineering - ShareGate
description: Company Description Workleap is a Montreal-based tech company, founded in 2006. We're builders at heart, we make simple products that actually matter to the people who use them. We have two product lines: Workleap Agent , our newest solution built to make every manager more effective, and ShareGate , the world's leading solution for Microsoft 365 migration and governance. More than 15,000 companies worldwide trust us to do exactly that. We're intentional about who joins us. If you're the kind of person who gets excited by a hard problem and wants to help shape what comes next, there's a place for you here. Your role ShareGate’s customers generate rich signals (product usage, support interactions, renewal dates), but those signals aren’t yet connected into an engine that protects and grows the revenue we already have. As our GTM Architect, Expansion & Retention, you’ll design, build and ship AI agents and agentic workflows that turn those signals into saved renewals and cross-sell pipeline. This is an embedded engineering role within GTM, not back-office ops: you’ll apply the signal-based, agent-first approach we already use for new customer acquisition to the customers we already have. Your impact: Protect renewals by building AI agents that continuously monitor renewal health and flag at-risk accounts to Account Managers early, with context, recommended next steps and enough lead time to act. Grow revenue from our existing customers by designing and running an agentic cross-sell motion: score fit for our second product line, research each account, personalize outreach, qualify interest and route genuine intent to the right salesperson with the full context needed to close. Define the signals your agents need and partner with Revenue Systems, which builds and owns the data flow between product usage and the CRM. Validate the data with SQL before you act on it. Replace manual workflows with AI agents and reusable pipeline modules (not one-off automations) that Account Management and Sales can run and own on their own. Tune both motions by owning reporting on pipeline generated, conversion, renewal outcomes and revenue impact, and by running controlled experiments without adding headcount. Drive adoption by turning everything you build into SOPs, demos and playbooks, so the team uses what you ship, not just appreciates it. Your team You’ll join a GTM engineering effort that already runs a signal-based, agent-first approach to new customer acquisition, and now points it at the customers we already have. The challenge: connect usage, support and renewal signals into agents that reduce the friction between signal and action. The tools, plays and channels will evolve; that mission won’t. Our stack: low-code orchestration (n8n, Make, Zapier or similar), Python or TypeScript, SQL on our data warehouse, and our CRM (HubSpot). What you'll bring Background in RevOps, GTM/marketing operations, customer success operations or GTM engineering, with hands-on experience building automation; Hands-on experience with low-code orchestration (n8n, Make, Zapier or similar), plus working knowledge of Python or TypeScript for API integrations and data transformation; fluency with agentic tools and MCP connectors. Strong LLM workflow design (agent orchestration, tool use, evaluation), sound judgment on when AI adds leverage versus complexity, and a track record of shipping AI agents or LLM workflows to real users, not just prototypes; Working SQL to query and validate usage, support and renewal data., so you can build and trust the data behind your agents; CRM fluency (HubSpot a plus): enough to design agents on our data model and work with Revenue Systems on what you need. Understanding of subscription business metrics (renewal rate, net retention, customer lifetime value), and experience with or strong interest in outbound and signal-based go-to-market motions; The ability to work directly with Sales and Account Management, translate complex builds into plain language, and earn adoption through demos and handoff docs, without a PM to bridge the gap; Bonus: experience building AI-driven qualification or scoring systems; a B2B SaaS background with multiple product lines, ideally product-led or demo-led; published technical content that makes complex systems accessible. raw.jobDescription:
Company Description

Workleap is a Montreal-based tech company, founded in 2006. We're builders at heart, we make simple products that actually matter to the people who use them. We have two product lines: Workleap Agent, our newest solution built to make every manager more effective, and ShareGate, the world's leading solution for Microsoft 365 migration and governance. More than 15,000 companies worldwide trust us to do exactly that. We're intentional about who joins us. If you're the kind of person who gets excited by a hard problem and wants to help shape what comes next, there's a place for you here.

Your role

ShareGate’s customers generate rich signals (product usage, support interactions, renewal dates), but those signals aren’t yet connected into an engine that protects and grows the revenue we already have. As our GTM Architect, Expansion & Retention, you’ll design, build and ship AI agents and agentic workflows that turn those signals into saved renewals and cross-sell pipeline. This is an embedded engineering role within GTM, not back-office ops: you’ll apply the signal-based, agent-first approach we already use for new customer acquisition to the customers we already have.

Your impact:

  • Protect renewals by building AI agents that continuously monitor renewal health and flag at-risk accounts to Account Managers early, with context, recommended next steps and enough lead time to act.
  • Grow revenue from our existing customers by designing and running an agentic cross-sell motion: score fit for our second product line, research each account, personalize outreach, qualify interest and route genuine intent to the right salesperson with the full context needed to close.
  • Define the signals your agents need and partner with Revenue Systems, which builds and owns the data flow between product usage and the CRM. Validate the data with SQL before you act on it.
  • Replace manual workflows with AI agents and reusable pipeline modules (not one-off automations) that Account Management and Sales can run and own on their own.
  • Tune both motions by owning reporting on pipeline generated, conversion, renewal outcomes and revenue impact, and by running controlled experiments without adding headcount.
  • Drive adoption by turning everything you build into SOPs, demos and playbooks, so the team uses what you ship, not just appreciates it.

Your team

You’ll join a GTM engineering effort that already runs a signal-based, agent-first approach to new customer acquisition, and now points it at the customers we already have. The challenge: connect usage, support and renewal signals into agents that reduce the friction between signal and action. The tools, plays and channels will evolve; that mission won’t.

Our stack: low-code orchestration (n8n, Make, Zapier or similar), Python or TypeScript, SQL on our data warehouse, and our CRM (HubSpot).

What you'll bring

  • Background in RevOps, GTM/marketing operations, customer success operations or GTM engineering, with hands-on experience building automation;
  • Hands-on experience with low-code orchestration (n8n, Make, Zapier or similar), plus working knowledge of Python or TypeScript for API integrations and data transformation;
  • fluency with agentic tools and MCP connectors. Strong LLM workflow design (agent orchestration, tool use, evaluation), sound judgment on when AI adds leverage versus complexity, and a track record of shipping AI agents or LLM workflows to real users, not just prototypes;
  • Working SQL to query and validate usage, support and renewal data., so you can build and trust the data behind your agents;
  • CRM fluency (HubSpot a plus): enough to design agents on our data model and work with Revenue Systems on what you need.
  • Understanding of subscription business metrics (renewal rate, net retention, customer lifetime value), and experience with or strong interest in outbound and signal-based go-to-market motions;
  • The ability to work directly with Sales and Account Management, translate complex builds into plain language, and earn adoption through demos and handoff docs, without a PM to bridge the gap;
  • Bonus: experience building AI-driven qualification or scoring systems; a B2B SaaS background with multiple product lines, ideally product-led or demo-led; published technical content that makes complex systems accessible.

Most of this sounds like you? Apply.

What the job comes with

  • Base salary: $110,000 - $140,000. This range reflects our Canada-wide compensation scale. Final offers may be adjusted based on the candidate's region to align with local market conditions.
    • OTE: $120,000 - $155,000
  • LTIP program, share in Workleap's long-term growth.
  • RRSP + Family health insurance + telemedicine + annual wellness budget.
  • Flexible vacation policy.
  • Remote work, with access to our Montreal office.
  • In-person gathering twice a year.
  • Claude access, for everyone.

Note: The internal title for this role is GTM Architect.

What drives us

At Workleap, we build software that sits at the center of how people experience work, every day, at every level.

We move fast. Priorities shift, decisions get made with the information we have, and we iterate. If you thrive on intensity and ambiguity doesn't slow you down, you'll feel right at home.
We're builders. We do what it takes to move forward. AI is part of our toolkit. We use it to go faster and decide smarter, not to replace judgment.

If you want real impact and a place where your decisions matter, this is it.

How we hire

Transparency is how we hire — for you as much as for us.

Here's how it works: a first call with a recruiter, then a virtual interview with the hiring manager. You'll then complete a take-home case study, followed by a meet with future colleagues to discuss it together. Depending on the role, the process may vary slightly — your recruiter will walk you through it on your first call.

We use AI to support certain steps of the process, but every hiring decision remains human.

We can't wait to meet you.

By applying, you confirm that you have read and agree to our privacy policy.

Familiarity in enterprise security solutions such as LDAP or Kerberos. Hands-on experience with Data Quality, Data Pipelines, Data Orchestration, and/or Job Control tools. Knowledgeable of at least least two or three of the following: data management processes, including data governance, data stewardship, master data management, data cataloging, and business rules management Proficiency in leveraging APIs via Java, Python, or similar scripting language for custom software implementations in Enterprise Linux or Unix environments. Always customer-focused and personally hold yourself accountable for the customer’s success. Masterful at troubleshooting, navigating, and facilitating resolution of challenging client connectivity and technical software issues. Joining Collibra’s Public Sector team

At Collibra Public Sector, our Professional Services team relies on Federal Solution Architects to deliver on customer expectations for the services we sell, working directly with customer key projects stakeholders throughout the entire customer journey. Ensuring growth, adoption and renewal, Federal Solution Architects act as customer champions, ensuring customers are onboarded and realizing value rapidly.

Senior Enterprise Solution Architects at Collibra Public Sector are responsible for

  • Supporting federal customer engagements by delivering mission-aligned architectural design and execution of Collibra products that adhere to Collibra Public Sector’s Delivery Models, Engagement Processes, Methodologies, and Artifacts, while ensuring compliance with applicable government regulations and security standards (e.g., FedRAMP, FISMA, GovCloud).
  • Providing federal agencies with tailored data governance strategies that incorporate best practices, enable knowledge transfer, and drive measurable business and mission outcomes.
  • Partnering cross-functionally with Collibra Sales, Customer Engineering, Product, Support, and Executive teams to ensure alignment with federal acquisition cycles and stakeholder priorities.
  • Identifying opportunities to expand Collibra’s footprint within agencies by aligning product capabilities to evolving agency mandates, modernization efforts, and compliance requirements.
  • Meeting or exceeding utilization goals in support of federal client success, long-term program engagement, and repeatable delivery excellence.
  • Contributing to the growth of Collibra’s public sector services and licensing business through account expansion, strategic planning, and customer advocacy.

You have

  • Because this role supports the U.S. government, it is required that the candidate be a US citizen who resides on US soil candidate and holds an active Top Secret Polygraph Lifestyle Security Clearance
  • Located in Chantilly, Virginia or the surrounding area.
  • Willing to be on site 100% of the time.
  • 3+ years of consulting experience supporting U.S. federal agencies with knowledge in the areas of Data Governance or Data Management.
  • An understanding of the leading PaaS providers, Data Lakes, Databases, and Integration platforms commonly adopted by federal agencies.
  • A minimum of 2 years of experience working with cloud platforms, network-based API integration (REST/JSON), and deployment automation.
  • Linux CLI proficiency.
  • Hands-on experience with AWS/Azure, Kubernetes, infrastructure and platform.
  • Experience with big data technologies such as Spark, and Hadoop.
  • Familiarity in enterprise security solutions such as LDAP or Kerberos.
  • Hands-on experience with Data Quality, Data Pipelines, Data Orchestration, and/or Job Control tools.
  • Knowledgeable of at least least two or three of the following: data management processes, including data governance, data stewardship, master data management, data cataloging, and business rules management
  • Proficiency in leveraging APIs via Java, Python, or similar scripting language for custom software implementations in Enterprise Linux or Unix environments.
  • Experience with data warehousing, ETL, data integration.
  • Skilled in developing functional and technical specifications.
  • Experienced with Collibra or comparable technologies.
  • A bachelor’s degree or equivalent related working experience is required.

You are

  • An effective communicator across business and technical stakeholders and able to tailor to different audiences.
  • Always customer-focused and personally hold yourself accountable for the customer’s success.
  • Masterful at troubleshooting, navigating, and facilitating resolution of challenging client connectivity and technical software issues.
  • Self-starting and interested in learning new software skills to support intricacies of Collibra’s application stack.
  • Able to work with business and IT owners to identify and align on solutions to data challenges, advocating for the importance of preserving data governance and quality.
  • Able to lead blueprinting, design workshops, and requirements gathering activities.

Measures of success

  • Within the first 30 days of employment, be able to
    • Present the services offered to your manager understanding the different deliverables and the value provided.
    • Present the Customer Journey framework to your manager understanding the different phases and roles and responsibilities within each phase.
    • Clearly understand the roles and responsibilities of all delivery personnel including an Engagement Manager, Solution Architect, Account Program Manager, Premium Support Engineer, Sales Engineer and Account Executive.
    • Work with the account team to build project plans aligned to each assigned account.
    • Have a baseline understanding of the Collibra product and associated features.
  • Within the first 60 days of employment
    • Clearly understand and present the functions and features of the product with your manager.
    • Show an intermediate understanding of the product with the ability to architect solutions.
  • Within the first 90 days of employment be able to
    • Execute on customer project plans based on product knowledge for assigned customers.
    • Understand and convey to customers how Collibra's suite product capabilities and the projects being delivered provide value to customers.
    • Design architectural solutions aligned with customer initiatives.

Compensation for this role

description: At Klaviyo, we value the unique backgrounds, experiences and perspectives each Klaviyo (we call ourselves Klaviyos) brings to our workplace each and every day. As our customers grow, our platform needs to support greater data volumes, more demanding workloads, and increasingly complex operations—with the performance and reliability they depend on. Engineering at this scale takes technical depth, sound judgment, and close collaboration. You’ll work across teams to solve challenging problems, turn architectural improvements into production results, and help build a platform ready for our largest customers. Your Impact We are seeking a senior technical leader to own Klaviyo’s approach to enterprise scalability, performance, reliability, and multi-region readiness. Reporting to a VP of Engineering, you will be a senior individual contributor with no direct reports. You will lead through technical expertise, hands-on engineering, and influence, partnering across teams to deliver improvements that matter to our customers. You will identify and remove major bottlenecks, drive platform-wide architectural changes, and establish clear measures of readiness for our largest tenants and most demanding workloads. Your work will span system design, profiling, implementation, and production rollout. You will also help teams adopt practical tools and repeatable patterns that make performance and reliability part of everyday engineering. This role suits an experienced engineer who can move between deep technical investigation and clear executive communication, make and defend architectural decisions, and build alignment across teams. Reports to: VP of Engineering Direct reports: None Location: Remote (Only applicable to candidates outside of MA. Requires travel to Boston HQ at least once per quarter) What You’ll Do Define what scale readiness means. Establish measurable targets for latency, throughput, error rates, and capacity. Build a shared scorecard and align teams on service-level objectives, error budgets, and performance expectations for critical enterprise workloads. Remove the bottlenecks that matter most. Use production data, profiling, and reproducible benchmarks to identify constraints. Partner with service owners to implement fixes and verify improvements under representative workloads. Drive architectural change. Design and implement sharding, partitioning, caching, back-pressure, and workload isolation strategies. Advance multi-region readiness and build safe paths for high-volume data migrations. Make scale engineering repeatable. Create lightweight benchmarks, profiling harnesses, and test environments that teams can use independently. Pair with engineers to turn successful fixes into reusable patterns. Build readiness into delivery. Lead scalability reviews and establish clear, proportionate release gates that surface risks early and help teams ship confidently. Turn incidents into lasting improvements. Lead technical deep dives, identify systemic causes, and work with teams to deliver and validate fixes that reduce recurring incidents. Apply AI where it improves outcomes. Use AI-assisted profiling, workload modeling, synthetic traffic, anomaly detection, and guided runbooks to improve investigation and response. Establish explicit guardrails, evaluate results, and measure operational impact. Connect engineering decisions to customer needs. Communicate priorities, tradeoffs, and results clearly to engineers and executives, tying technical investments to customer experience, enterprise growth, and operating efficiency. What You’ll Bring Deep experience scaling multi-tenant SaaS. You bring 12+ years of relevant engineering experience, with a track record of removing significant bottlenecks and demonstrating measurable production impact. Strong performance and distributed systems expertise. You have hands-on experience with performance engineering, capacity planning, sharding and partitioning, caching, back-pressure, tenant isolation, multi-region architectures, and large-scale migrations. Engineering depth from diagnosis through delivery. You can investigate unfamiliar systems, test hypotheses, write production code, and work with service owners to roll out changes safely. Sound technical judgment. You use evidence to weigh architectural tradeoffs and know when to address an immediate constraint versus invest in a broader platform change. Leadership across organizational boundaries. You align teams around shared outcomes, clarify ownership, and build practical standards that help engineers move faster. Clear communication. You explain complex technical decisions and their business implications to both engineering and executive audiences. Practical AI fluency. You have applied AI tools or automation to engineering work and can evaluate their usefulness, limitations, and operational risks. You are curious about new approaches and disciplined about validating them. What Success Looks Like in 6–12 Months A company-wide scale scorecard is adopted and reviewed regularly, with agreed targets and clear ownership for critical enterprise workloads. Two to three high-impact bottlenecks are removed, with reproducible benchmarks demonstrating sustained improvements. Our largest customer workloads show measurable improvements in tail latency, throughput, and error rates. Multi-region readiness and high-volume migration plans have clear priorities, tested assumptions, and actionable next steps. Teams use shared benchmarks and readiness checks to catch regressions earlier, and repeat P0 incidents decline. AI-assisted tools demonstrate measurable value in investigation or incident response, such as faster regression isolation or fewer noisy alerts, with appropriate controls and observability. title: CFO (Mitglied der Geschäftsleitung)
description: Das Universitäre Zentrum für Zahnmedizin Basel (UZB) vereint Patientenbehandlung, akademische Lehre und Forschung unter einem Dach. Mit rund 300 Mitarbeitenden, rund 100'000 Behandlungen pro Jahr und einem Umsatz von ca. CHF 40 Mio. erbringt das UZB seine Leistungen unter anderem auf Basis von Leistungsaufträgen mit der Universität Basel und dem Kanton Basel-Stadt. Wir suchen eine oder einen CFO mit überzeugenden betriebswirtschaftlichen und finanziellen Kenntnissen. Als Mitglied der Geschäftsleitung ist neben dem Finanzwissen auch unternehmerisches Denken und Handeln gefragt, um das Unternehmen gesamtheitlich zu steuern und weiterzuentwickeln. Ihre Verantwortung Sie verantworten die finanzielle Führung des UZB – von der Budget-, Liquiditäts- und Finanzplanung über das Rechnungswesen und die Rechnungslegung nach Swiss GAAP FER bis hin zum Controlling – und stellen ein aussagekräftiges, stufengerechtes Reporting an unsere Leitungserbringer, die Geschäftsleitung und den Verwaltungsrat sicher. Sie sichern die Finanzierung und Liquidität, entwickeln das Risikomanagement und das interne Kontrollsystem weiter und sind Ansprechperson für den Prüfungsausschuss des Verwaltungsrats und die Revisionsstelle. Sie führen und entwickeln die Bereiche Finanzen (rund 10 Mitarbeitende), IT (3), Technischer Dienst (3) und Einkauf mit vier direkt unterstellten Führungspersonen und fördern die Zusammenarbeit über Fachgrenzen hinweg. Sie bringen die Digitalisierung und Weiterentwicklung von Abläufen und Systemen voran und entscheiden bei der laufenden Evaluation einer neuen ERP-Lösung massgeblich mit. Als Mitglied der Geschäftsleitung tragen Sie auch die gesamtunternehmerische Verantwortung mit und bringen sich in Fragen der Unternehmensentwicklung aktiv ein. Sie beraten die CEO und die Geschäftsleitung als Sparringpartner in allen betriebswirtschaftlichen Fragen und erarbeiten Business Cases für neue Angebote und Projekte. Sie schaffen Entscheidungsgrundlagen für den Dialog mit internen und externen Anspruchsgruppen in einem öffentlich-rechtlich geprägten Umfeld und pflegen den Kontakt zu den relevanten Stakeholdern. Ihr beruflicher Hintergrund Sie verfügen über substanzielles Know-how in Finanzen und Controlling sowie über Erfahrung in einer verantwortlichen Finanzführungsfunktion. Sie haben einen (Fach-) Hochschulstudium in Betriebswirtschaft abgeschlossen oder sind Expertin bzw. Experte in Rechnungslegung und Controlling; Erfahrung mit Swiss GAAP FER und SAP ist von Vorteil. Sie haben Führungserfahrung, sind es gewohnt bei Entscheidungsprozessen mitzuwirken und anschliessend die Entscheidungen in ihrem Verantwortungsbereich konsequent umzusetzen. Sie kommunizieren differenziert und transparent, arbeiten pragmatisch und verbinden finanzielle Sorgfalt mit Offenheit für neue Lösungen. Sie verfügen über stilsichere Deutsch- und gute Englischkenntnisse. Sie interessieren sich für Digitalisierung und einen verantwortungsvollen Umgang mit Daten und neuen Technologien. Erfahrung im Gesundheitswesen oder in einer öffentlich-rechtlichen Organisation sind willkommen, doch keine Voraussetzung. Was die Aufgabe auszeichnet Das UZB ist eine dynamische Institution: 2016 gegründet und seit 2021 um rund 30 % gewachsen. Unsere Strukturen, Prozesse und Systeme lassen sich aktiv mitprägen. Sie verbinden eine finanzielle Schlüsselrolle mit der Möglichkeit, die Weiterentwicklung einer Unternehmung mit gesellschaftlichem Auftrag aus Geschäftsleitungsperspektive mitzugestalten. Die Position verlangt Nähe zum Tagesgeschäft ebenso wie einen verlässlichen Blick auf das Ganze. Interessiert? Vertraulicher Erstkontakt Sie möchten mehr erfahren? description: About Supabase Supabase is the Postgres development platform, built by developers for developers. We provide a complete backend solution including Database, Auth, Storage, Edge Functions, Realtime, and Vector Search. All services are deeply integrated and designed for growth. You'll work closely with the rest of the SDK team, our Auth, Realtime, Storage, PostgREST, Functions, CLI and Docs teams, and the open-source community, helping us make the Python SDK a library Python developers genuinely enjoy using. Python developers reach Supabase from backend services, data pipelines, notebooks, and a growing number of AI agents and agent frameworks. The Python SDK is how all of them talk to the platform: database queries, auth, storage, realtime and edge functions, in both sync and async flavors. This is a library-authoring role, and the work happens in the open: public repos, public issue trackers, and API decisions whose consequences last for years. If you get satisfaction from a type checker that catches the bug before your users do, from an async client that cleans up after itself, and from an issue tracker that isn't a graveyard, you'll like it here. This role is ideal for someone who thrives in async, fast-paced environments and is excited about building developer tools that scale to millions. What You'll Be Responsible For Build and evolve our Python SDK across database, auth, storage, realtime and functions, with both sync and async APIs that feel natural in Python. Start new things. Alongside the maintenance work, find what's missing, make the case for it, and build it. Nobody will hand you the list. Work in the open. Triage inbound issues, review and shepherd outside contributions, keep CI and release automation healthy, and hold a clear, kind line on scope. Own the typing experience. Make the SDK fully typed and checker-friendly, so autocomplete and static analysis stay correct in real codebases. Keep us honest across environments. Multiple Python versions, sync and async frameworks, workers, serverless and notebooks — with dependency ranges that don't fight our users' projects. Test it, don't assume it. Work on realtime. Long-lived websocket connections, reconnection, and subscription and presence semantics. Track the platform. Have authored or maintained a published library with a public API and users outside your own company. You know what it costs to change something people depend on. Know the maintainer side of open source. Issue triage at volume, reviewing outside PRs, release automation, changelogs and semver, security reports, and saying no to a feature request without losing the person who asked. Are fluent in asyncio and have opinions on how a library should serve both sync and async callers. Know Python packaging for libraries: pyproject.toml , wheels, modern tooling, version support policy, and why libraries shouldn't pin their dependencies tightly. Test as a habit: unit, type-level and end-to-end against a real stack. Every fix comes with a regression test. Write well. Design docs, changelogs and issue replies are a large part of the output here, much of it public, and we're async by default. Have real autonomy: you find the important work, scope it, ship it, and say what you didn't do. Communicate clearly across both technical and non-technical audiences Have experience in async or globally distributed teams Are energized by solving real-world problems for developers Are comfortable navigating ambiguity and moving quickly Bonus points if you: have run a major-version migration for a public package, know your way around JWT/OAuth, have built integrations for AI agent frameworks, or have generated idiomatic clients from a schema.
