title: Autonomous Systems Security Engineer
description: Headquarters: Remote-Friendly (Travel Required) | San Francisco, CA About Anthropic Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems. About the role Claude is trained and served on hardware in data centers Anthropic operates and in sites partners build and run for us. DCSE secures that footprint: the sites, the hardware moving through them, and the people and vendors who touch it. You'll be the engineer who owns autonomous systems across that footprint as one security domain, from both sides: drones, ground robots and automated vehicles for patrol, inspection and moving hardware, including the security of that automation inside secure areas, and the detection systems that tell us what is flying over or operating near a site uninvited. You set the approach, select and integrate the platforms and sensors, write the requirements vendors build to, and run what you ship, from the operating model where operators assign missions and machines carry them out to the playbook that turns a detection into an identified track and a well-evidenced handoff to whoever holds authority over the airspace. Interdiction is not part of this role. The goal is security that runs itself: coverage, fleet health and evidence verified continuously, with tools and AI agents doing the routine triage. We favor simple, standard controls and tools that can be verified over elaborate ones. We use Claude throughout our engineering workflow and expect you to as well. You'll work with the rest of DCSE, including its physical security systems engineers and the engineers on its security monitoring platform, with Anthropic's data center operations and legal teams, and directly with site operators, equipment vendors and aviation and public safety authorities. The role is based in San Francisco, with remote applicants in the US considered, and involves regular travel to data center sites, which are critical infrastructure. Key responsibilities Autonomous security and inspection systems: own the drones, ground robots and other autonomous platforms for perimeter patrol, incident response and infrastructure inspection: platform selection, operating model, operator qualification, maintenance, and the data path from machine to analyst Tools, automation and AI agents: build the integrations that carry detections, tracks, telemetry and fleet health into the team's security monitoring platform, and the tools and agents that triage detections, check fleet health and assemble evidence. When a review keeps costing people time, you build the tool or agent that retires it Detection of uncrewed systems: engineer the sensing that tells us what is flying over or operating near a site, what it is and who needs to know: sensor selection and evaluation against live targets, per-site coverage, classification and false-alarm handling, and the playbook from first detection to handoff, with evidence retained Security of site automation: engineer the controls on automated vehicles, robots and similar machines that move hardware or work inside secure areas: identity and access, network isolation, what they may record and where it goes, fail-secure behavior, their place in chain of custody, and acceptance before they enter a site Regulatory and site constraints: establish what we may sense, fly, drive, record and retain at each site, partner-operated sites included, under the aviation, spectrum, privacy and safety rules that apply there, with the waivers and approvals that extend it and coordination with local authorities set up before it is needed Health monitoring: define and test heartbeats, loss-of-coverage and lost-link alarms and fail-secure behavior, so a silent sensor or machine shows as a fault, not a quiet day Vendor requirements and acceptance: write the requirements, evaluate against live flights and runs, and hold vendors to what they ship Minimum qualifications Have engineered autonomous or sensing systems in the field (drones, ground robots, automated vehicles, or RF, radar or optical detection sensors): selected, integrated or secured them for an operation other people relied on, and verified what they actually do against real targets or runs rather than a datasheet Have integrated systems you did not build (vendor APIs, SDKs, appliances, machine and sensor telemetry) into a platform that outlives any one of them Read and review code, design the data systems behind security tooling, and build automation (often with AI coding agents) using Git and code review Have done this work hands-on for data centers, critical infrastructure or a large hardware fleet Have designed inside a regulatory or safety constraint (aviation, spectrum, privacy, machine safety or similar) and can show the decision it drove Own a domain end to end: set the approach, carry it through with vendors, site operators, partners and authorities, and run it as something people depend on every day Preferred qualifications Remote pilot certification (for example FAA Part 107) and experience flying beyond visual line of sight under a waiver or exemption Experience with counter-drone (counter-UAS) detection, airspace surveillance or air traffic data systems Experience running a robot, drone or automated-vehicle fleet in an industrial, logistics or data center setting: fleet management, mission planning, safety cases Experience securing embedded, operational technology or robotic systems: device identity, network segmentation, update control, logging Experience with physical security operations at large sites, with law enforcement or aviation authorities, or at sites you did not fully control: cloud, colocation or GPU cloud operators Have built AI agents or automation that replaced recurring manual work The annual compensation range for this role is listed below. For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role. Annual Salary: $320,000 — $405,000 USD Logistics Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices. Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this. We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team. Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings. How we're different We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills. The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences. Come work with us! Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. Guidance on Candidates' AI Usage: Learn about our policy for using AI in our application process. To apply: https://weworkremotely.com/remote-jobs/anthropic-autonomous-systems-security-engineer

raw.title: Carrot: Sr. IT Systems Engineer
raw.description:
Headquarters: Remote

About Carrot:

Carrot is the leading global fertility and family care platform, built on intelligent care orchestration: the right clinical guidance, at the right moment, in the context of each member’s life. More than a thousand multinational employers, health plans, and health systems trust Carrot to support millions of members across 195 countries – from pre-pregnancy through menopause and major life moments in between. Carrot's comprehensive clinical program delivers industry-leading cost savings for plan sponsors and award-winning experiences and improved outcomes for millions of people worldwide.

Carrot is widely regarded as a defining force in healthcare innovation as a recipient of several top-tier awards, including Fast Company's 'Most Innovative Companies' and CNBC's '100 Barrier Breaking Startups'. The company is regularly cited by leading global outlets — including The Economist, Bloomberg, The Wall Street Journal, NPR, ABC News, and Harvard Business Review — as a leading voice on digital health, the future of work, and family health. Learn more at get-carrot.com.

The Opportunity 

Carrot is looking for a Sr. IT Systems Engineer to design, scale, and secure the identity, endpoint, and SaaS platforms that power our global, remote-first workforce. You will set the technical direction for how employees and devices connect to Carrot systems, while staying hands-on in the tooling, automation, and complex problem-solving that make IT reliable at scale.

This role sits at the center of IT engineering. You will lead larger initiatives from design through rollout, partner closely with Information Security on zero-trust and compliance priorities, and raise the bar for the rest of the team through standards, documentation, and mentorship. If you want broad technical ownership, influence over the IT roadmap, and the chance to build systems that grow with a high-growth healthcare company, this role was built for that.

What You’ll Own

In this role, you will:

  • Architect and own Carrot's identity, endpoint, and SaaS platforms, including Okta, JAMF, Intune, and Google Workspace, with a focus on security, reliability, and user experience
  • Lead design and rollout of larger IT initiatives, such as zero-trust access models, device compliance frameworks, and global endpoint standards
  • Build and maintain automation and infrastructure as code that manage configuration, provisioning, and lifecycle workflows at scale
  • Partner with Information Security to design controls, drive vulnerability management, and keep Carrot audit-ready for SOC 2, HIPAA, and customer security reviews
  • Serve as the senior technical escalation point, leading incident response and root cause analysis for complex or high-impact issues
  • Define engineering standards, runbooks, and documentation, and mentor IT teammates to grow their technical depth
  • Evaluate vendors and tools, build business cases, and make clear recommendations on build versus buy tradeoffs
  • Design environments that support global care and operations teams, including secure and efficient remote computing setups
  • Contribute to the IT roadmap and communicate priorities, risks, and progress to technical and business stakeholders

What Success Looks Like  

In your first 12–18 months, you will have:

  • Established a clear, documented architecture and standards for identity, endpoint, and SaaS management that the team can build on
  • Delivered at least one major platform initiative, such as a zero-trust access model or endpoint modernization, with measurable gains in security posture and employee experience
  • Reduced manual IT work through automation and infrastructure as code, with a measurable drop in recurring ticket volume
  • Strengthened audit readiness, contributing to clean results on security and compliance reviews
  • Raised the technical capability of the team through mentorship, documentation, and shared standards
  • Built trusted partnerships with Information Security, People, Engineering, and Finance

About You

You likely have:

  • 6+ years of experience in IT systems engineering, endpoint engineering, or infrastructure roles, including ownership of production platforms
  • Deep, hands-on expertise with identity and access platforms such as Okta, including SSO, SCIM, lifecycle automation, and conditional access
  • Expert-level experience managing Mac and Windows fleets with JAMF and Intune, including packaging, deployment, security policy, and compliance enforcement
  • Strong scripting and automation skills (for example Python, Bash, or PowerShell), with experience using APIs and source-controlled configuration
  • Experience designing and implementing security controls, such as encryption, vulnerability management, and zero-trust principles, in partnership with Security teams
  • A track record of leading cross-functional technical projects from design through rollout without direct authority
  • Experience mentoring or technically guiding other engineers
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to translate complex tradeoffs for executive and non-technical audiences

Nice to Have ⭐

While not required, we would be especially excited if you bring:

  • Experience in healthcare, health tech, or another regulated environment (for example, HIPAA or SOC 2)
  • Experience with infrastructure as code and CI/CD practices applied to endpoint or SaaS configuration
  • Hands-on experience with AWS or GCP and modern cloud networking concepts
  • Experience designing remote computing environments for call center or clinical operations teams, such as VDI or managed browser models
  • Experience building AI-assisted workflows or tooling to improve IT operations
  • Relevant certifications (for example JAMF Certified Expert, Okta Certified Professional, or Microsoft Endpoint Administrator)

Why This Role Matters

Every Carrot employee depends on technology that is secure, reliable, and easy to use, whether they are supporting members through deeply personal care journeys or partnering with global employers. This role sets the technical foundation that makes that possible.

As Carrot continues to scale across geographies and functions, the architecture and standards you establish will protect member trust, strengthen our security posture, and give the business the speed and confidence to keep growing.

Why Candidates Join Carrot

Carrot offers the opportunity to do meaningful work in service of a deeply human mission.

Highlights include:

  • A mission-driven company focused on expanding access to fertility and family-forming care globally.
  • A high-growth environment where leaders are empowered to shape strategy and drive impact.
  • Competitive compensation, equity, and comprehensive benefits.
  • Flexible Time Off and a culture that actively encourages employees to recharge.
  • Comprehensive parental leave and family-forming benefits.
  • A collaborative, inclusive, and values-driven culture.
  • The opportunity to work alongside passionate, thoughtful teammates committed to improving healthcare outcomes worldwide.

 

Compensation

Carrot offers a holistic Total Rewards package designed to support our employees in all aspects of their lives inside and outside of work, including health and wellness benefits, retirement savings plans, short- and long-term incentives, parental leave, family-forming assistance, and a competitive compensation package.

  • Base Salary Range: $150,000 – $175,000 (primary range).
  • Geo-Tier Adjustment: Up to $190,000 for highly experienced candidates within 50 miles of San Francisco, NYC, or Seattle.

Actual compensation may vary from the posted base salary depending on your confirmed job-related skills and experience.

description: Headquarters: -REMOTE, BULGARIA- For over 20 years, Smartsheet has empowered teams to manage work seamlessly and scale solutions smarter. Our team collaboratively operates Smartsheet's high-performance edge proxy platform and drives the adoption of internal engineering tooling. The edge proxy serves as the entry point for all traffic across Smartsheet's commercial and FedRAMP-authorized US Government environments. The team supports the lifecycle of this platform: from maintaining proxy configurations, to provisioning the multi-region AWS EKS infrastructure it runs on, to assisting with observability. Beyond the edge layer, the team also drives the integration of internal developer tooling — from а developer portal (IDP) to standardized CI/CD pipelines — that improves the engineering experience and velocity across the company. Operate Kubernetes clusters: Assist in managing multi-region EKS deployments via GitOps workflows (e.g., FluxCD, ArgoCD) and Helm charts. Support CI/CD pipelines: Help design, maintain, and improve shared GitLab CI/CD pipeline templates used across team repositories, embedding DevSecOps guardrails. Automate operational toil: Build tooling for tasks such as container image patching, EKS AMI rotation, and automated patching cycles. Manage observability: Help provision and maintain Datadog SLOs, monitors, and dashboards; participate in the team's on-call rotation responding to incidents. Support Developer Experience initiatives: Assist in the rollout and integration of various platforms to reduce cognitive load for engineering teams. Apply AI tools: Leverage AI-based workflows within your domain to improve project execution, infrastructure design, and debugging. You Have: 2–4 years of experience in DevOps, Platform Engineering, or Site Reliability Engineering. A BS or MS in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent industry experience. Hands-on experience with Terraform for managing cloud infrastructure. Experience with Kubernetes operations and AWS services (EKS, VPC, IAM, ECR). Proficiency in at least one general-purpose programming language — Go or Python preferred — for building operational automation. Experience designing or maintaining CI/CD pipelines (GitLab CI/CD preferred). Familiarity with container image security practices and GitOps workflows. A strong operational mindset with a willingness to participate in on-call rotations and incident response. Excellent verbal and written communication skills. Fluency in English is required. Familiarity with leveraging AI-based workflows to author or maintain code/infrastructure. Legally eligible to work in Bulgaria on an ongoing basis. Nice to Have: Understanding of reverse proxies, API gateways, or load balancers (NGINX, HAProxy, or equivalent). Familiarity with FedRAMP or AWS GovCloud operational constraints. Experience managing Datadog resources via infrastructure as code. Experience integrating internal developer portals or feature flag management tools. Smartsheet provides a competitive base salary range for roles that may be hired in different geographic areas we are licensed to operate our business from. Actual compensation is determined by several factors including, but not limited to, level of professional, educational experience, skills, and specific candidate location. In addition, this role will be eligible for a market-competitive incentive opportunity. Get to Know Us: At Smartsheet, your ideas are heard, your potential is supported, and your contributions have real impact. You’ll have the freedom to explore, push boundaries, and grow beyond your role. We welcome diverse perspectives and nontraditional paths—because we know that impact comes from individuals who care deeply and challenge thoughtfully. When you’re doing work that stretches you, excites you, and connects you to something bigger, that’s magic at work. Let’s build what’s next, together. Experience with LLM/AI features in production (guardrails, logging, security considerations). Implement logging, monitor performance, and ship production-quality code. Datadog and Sentry experience is a plus. Collaborate directly with the Senior AI & Design Lead for clear ownership, feedback, and iteration. Maintain clear documentation of architecture, decisions, and interfaces for internal teams. (Bonus) Use Convex or similar BaaS / serverless data platforms for rapid product delivery. (Bonus) Build and maintain n8n workflows (webhooks, scheduled jobs, error workflows, credential management, self-hosting) to automate internal operations and connect our product stack. This is mandatory; applications without this disclosure will not be considered. What we’re looking for 3+ years of experience as a full-stack or frontend-heavy engineer. Strong proficiency in React , Next.js , TypeScript/JavaScript. Hands-on experience with AWS for production workloads. Solid understanding of web security best practices (OWASP, secure storage, encryption in transit/at rest, secrets management). Experience building systems in or adjacent to healthcare, education, or compliance-heavy environments is a plus. Excellent async communication, code ownership, and ability to work with a small, senior-led team. Comfort working from a clear product brief and also proposing improvements proactively. Familiarity with logging, monitoring, and observability tools. Take-home assignment (Step 1 of the process) Please complete a take-home assignment. You are allowed to use LLMs to write code. To ensure that your work will not be used at Fluence, we’ve made it unrelated to healthcare: Build “LendLoop”: a neighborhood tool-lending board with automated workflows A simple app where neighbors list tools they are willing to lend, request to borrow from each other, and receive automated notifications and reminders handled by n8n. Stack Next.js (App Router) Clerk for authentication Convex for data + backend logic n8n (self-hosted via Docker or n8n Cloud) for workflow automation TypeScript Requirements Public page The fictional company name is LendLoop . Short tagline, e.g. “Borrow what you need. Lend what you don’t.” Show: A read-only list of available tools (name and category only, no owner details), pulled from Convex. A “Sign in to lend or borrow” button wired to Clerk. Approve or decline requests on their own tools. Mark a loan as returned. Show: All tools with availability status, filterable by category. “My listings”, “My requests”, and “Incoming requests” views. Nice, minimal layout. Roles & rules Have two roles: admin : Can remove any listing, view all loans, and mark a lender as “Trusted Lender”. user : Can create, edit, and delete only their own listings, and act only on requests involving their own tools or their own borrowing. Implement the above role-based access control with best practices, enforced in Convex functions, not only in the UI. Automation with n8n Build at least two n8n workflows: Request notification: when a borrow request is created or changes status, Convex calls an n8n Webhook. The workflow notifies the relevant user (email, Slack, Discord, or a logged mock notification is fine) using only the fields it needs. Overdue reminders: a scheduled workflow runs daily, fetches overdue loans from a Convex HTTP endpoint, sends a reminder to each borrower, and writes the reminder status back to Convex. Secure the integration in both directions: Sign webhook payloads (e.g. HMAC with a shared secret) and verify signatures on the receiving side. Keep secrets in environment variables and n8n credentials, never in code or exported workflow JSON. Make write-backs idempotent so retries do not create duplicate records or reminders. Handle failures with retries and an error workflow (or equivalent) so failed runs are visible and never fail silently. (Bonus) Show recent automation activity on each loan in the app, e.g. “Reminder sent 2 days ago”. Deliverables A GitHub repository with the app source code. Exported n8n workflow JSON files in the repository. A README covering local setup (including n8n, e.g. a docker-compose file), environment variables, architecture, and your security and data-minimization decisions. title: Principal Data Engineer
description: Headquarters: Remote-US ZoomInfo is where careers accelerate. We move fast, think boldly, and empower you to do the best work of your life. You’ll be surrounded by teammates who care deeply, challenge each other, and celebrate wins. With tools that amplify your impact and a culture that backs your ambition, you won’t just contribute. You’ll make things happen fast. We are seeking a highly experienced, hands-on Principal Data Engineer to define and evolve the architecture, engineering standards, and operating model for our enterprise data platform. This role is for a technical leader who excels at complex system design: translating business and analytical needs into scalable, reliable, secure, and maintainable data products. The Principal Data Engineer will lead critical architectural decisions across data ingestion, storage, transformation, orchestration, governance, observability, and consumption, while raising the engineering bar through mentorship, design reviews, and pragmatic best practices. You will work across engineering, analytics, platform, security, and business stakeholders to create systems that make trusted data accessible, timely, and actionable at scale. What You’ll Do Lead Data Architecture and System Design Own the technical vision and architecture for scalable, resilient, and cost-effective data platforms and pipelines. Design end-to-end data systems spanning batch and streaming ingestion, transformation, data modeling, storage, orchestration, serving layers, and consumption patterns. Make and document high-quality architecture decisions, including tradeoffs involving performance, reliability, scalability, latency, security, maintainability, and cost. Define reusable architectural patterns for common data engineering challenges, including CDC, event-driven data flows, schema evolution, slowly changing dimensions, data quality, and multi-tenant or domain-oriented data models. Establish clear boundaries and interfaces between operational systems, data platforms, analytics layers, and downstream applications. Lead technical design reviews for high-impact initiatives and provide clear, constructive direction on implementation approaches. Identify architectural risks early and drive plans to mitigate technical debt, single points of failure, data inconsistency, and operational fragility. Set Engineering Standards and Best Practices Establish and continuously improve standards for data engineering development, testing, deployment, documentation, monitoring, incident response, and lifecycle management. Define best practices for version-controlled data transformations, infrastructure as code, CI/CD, code review, automated testing, and environment promotion. Build a culture of data reliability by implementing standards for data contracts, schema management, lineage, observability, freshness, completeness, accuracy, and reconciliation. Champion security, privacy, access control, governance, retention, and compliance requirements throughout the data lifecycle. Develop practical engineering guardrails that enable teams to move quickly without sacrificing quality, trust, or operational excellence. Drive adoption of well-defined SLIs, SLOs, alerting, runbooks, and post-incident learning practices for critical data products. Drive Technical Decision-Making Serve as a trusted technical authority for complex, cross-functional decisions involving data architecture, tooling, platform capabilities, and engineering investments. Facilitate technical discussions that turn ambiguous requirements into durable, well-reasoned solutions. Evaluate build-versus-buy decisions, platform technologies, and vendor capabilities using clear criteria and documented recommendations. Align architecture decisions with organizational priorities, business outcomes, data strategy, and long-term platform sustainability. Create and maintain architecture decision records, reference architectures, roadmaps, and technical standards that provide clarity across teams. Influence leaders and stakeholders through concise communication of technical options, risks, tradeoffs, and recommended paths forward. Build and Improve Data Products Lead the design and development of high-value, production-grade data pipelines, datasets, and platform capabilities. Partner with data analysts, data scientists, software engineers, and product teams to deliver well-modeled, discoverable, and trustworthy data products. Optimize data systems for reliability, usability, performance, scalability, and cost efficiency. Drive modernization initiatives, including migration from legacy platforms, consolidation of fragmented pipelines, and reduction of manual operational processes. Ensure data products are designed with clear ownership, documentation, lineage, quality expectations, and support models. Mentor and Multiply Engineering Excellence Mentor data engineers at all levels, with a particular focus on growing senior engineers into strong technical leaders. Provide practical coaching on system design, data modeling, debugging, performance tuning, code quality, and production operations. Lead architecture reviews, technical workshops, design sessions, and knowledge-sharing forums. Establish reusable templates, reference implementations, and playbooks that improve consistency and accelerate delivery. Foster an inclusive, high-accountability engineering culture centered on thoughtful collaboration, continuous learning, and ownership. Act as a technical multiplier: helping teams make better decisions independently while maintaining alignment with shared architectural principles. What you bring Required 10+ years of experience in software engineering, data engineering, platform engineering, or a related technical discipline. 5+ years designing and operating large-scale data platforms, distributed data systems, or enterprise-grade data products. Demonstrated expertise in end-to-end system design, including defining requirements, evaluating tradeoffs, designing resilient architectures, and delivering production systems. Deep experience with modern data architecture concepts, such as lakehouse or warehouse platforms, batch and streaming processing, data modeling, orchestration, metadata management, and data governance. Strong proficiency in SQL and at least one general-purpose programming language, such as Python, Java, Scala, or similar. Experience with distributed data processing frameworks and technologies such as Spark, Kafka, Flink, Snowflake, Databricks, BigQuery, Redshift, or equivalent platforms. Strong knowledge of data modeling practices across analytical, operational, and domain-oriented use cases. Experience establishing engineering standards for testing, CI/CD, observability, infrastructure as code, reliability, and security. Proven ability to lead technical decisions across multiple teams without relying on direct authority. Exceptional written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to explain complex technical concepts and tradeoffs to technical and non-technical stakeholders. Demonstrated experience mentoring engineers and raising technical standards across an organization. Preferred Experience with cloud-native data platforms on AWS, Azure, or GCP. Experience implementing data mesh, domain-oriented data product, or self-service platform patterns. Familiarity with data governance, cataloging, lineage, privacy, and access-control tooling. Experience supporting financial, revenue, operational, customer, or enterprise analytics domains. Experience with ML data pipelines, feature stores, or AI/LLM data foundations. Experience managing major data-platform migrations, modernization programs, or large-scale architectural transformations. Leadership Competencies Systems thinker : Connects individual technical decisions to broader platform, organizational, and business outcomes. Pragmatic architect : Balances ideal-state architecture with incremental delivery and operational realities. Technical judgment : Makes clear recommendations amid ambiguity and communicates tradeoffs transparently. Builder and operator : Designs for production from the beginning, including reliability, security, observability, and supportability. Mentor and multiplier : Develops others and creates scalable mechanisms for technical excellence. Collaborative influencer : Builds alignment across engineering, analytics, security, product, and business teams. Our Technology Stack Languages & Databases: Python, SQL, MySQL, NoSQL databases Orchestration & Transformation: Airflow, dbt Data Platforms: Snowflake, AWS, GCP, BigQuery, Redshift Data Integration: Fivetran, custom ETL/ELT frameworks Observability & Data Reliability: Datadog, monitoring, alerting, data-quality frameworks #LI-JH1 #LI-Remote Actual compensation offered will be based on factors such as the candidate’s work location, qualifications, skills, experience and/or training. Your recruiter can share more information about the specific salary range for your desired work location during the hiring process. We want our employees and their families to thrive. In addition to comprehensive benefits we offer holistic mind, body and lifestyle programs designed for overall well-being. Learn more about ZoomInfo benefits here . Below is the US base salary for this position. Additional compensation such as Bonus, Commission, Equity and other benefits may also apply. $171,500 — $269,500 USD About us: ZoomInfo (NASDAQ: GTM), the all-in-one AI GTM platform, enables sales, marketing, and customer success teams to execute their go-to-market strategy with confidence. Powered by the industry's most comprehensive B2B data, including more than 100 million companies, 500 million contacts, and billions of signals, ZoomInfo delivers the intelligence, automation, and integrations that modern revenue teams need to identify, engage, and convert their best buyers. ZoomInfo is committed to protecting your privacy when you apply for jobs with us. Please review our Job Applicant Privacy Notice for more details on how we handle your personal information. We also consider qualified candidates with criminal histories in accordance with legal requirements. For Massachusetts Applicants: It is unlawful in Massachusetts to require or administer a lie detector test as a condition of employment or continued employment. Headquarters: Remote • Canada

About Upsun

Upsun is the software factory for human-AI workflows. We give teams one unified platform to create, review, deploy, and run software, with AI agents and humans working in sync. Developers, DevOps engineers, and platform teams use Upsun to build and ship with confidence, without wrestling with infrastructure.

Upsun brings this together through two products: one that shapes the work, and one that runs it.

  • Upsun Dispatch™: the AI-first product accelerator. Dispatch governs and simplifies collaboration between AI agents and cross-functional human teams, so work gets shaped, reviewed, and moved to production faster. Ship better code, not just more code.
  • Upsun Cloud: the Cloud Application Platform for AI acceleration. Cloud is where that software runs. It helps organizations launch agentic software into production confidently and reliably, with:
    • Predictable performance, even at scale
    • Secure, compliant environments by default
    • Real-time observability and profiling built in
    • Cloning, configuration, and provisioning in seconds
    • Sandbox environments where AI agents can build and test safely

The name says it all. "Up" means uptime, reliability, and acceleration. "Sun" reflects our follow-the-sun-support, a 24x7, globally distributed support team keeping the lights on while you rest. Our core belief is that software should power brighter solutions and greater innovation. 

What's our commonality, our cultural fabric? A curious spirit and a thirst for knowledge; an eagerness for innovative ideas and cultures. We believe we can build anything together in an environment that frees you to do your best work.

Our values: 

We make a positive impact.

We aim for the stars.

We care for each other. 

Impact of a Senior IT Systems Engineer

As a Senior IT Engineer, you help shape and improve the systems that our 250+ person remote company relies on every day. Your work spans identity and access, Google Workspace, device management, and our wider SaaS environment.
Reporting to the IT Director, you take ownership of complex problems and lead improvements from initial assessment through delivery. You identify what needs attention, recommend priorities, and make thoughtful decisions that balance security, reliability, and employee experience. You also help the team build stronger practices through clear documentation, shared knowledge, and practical guidance.

What to expect

  • Identity platform: Improve our identity and access services, with Okta at the core. This includes single sign-on, automated account provisioning, multi-factor authentication, access policies, and emergency access. Work with IT and Security to make access secure, consistent, and straightforward.

  • Google Workspace: Lead the administration and improvement of our Google Workspace environment, including users, groups, Gmail, Drive, shared drives, and security settings. Improve how people collaborate, manage sharing and access, and keep our configuration aligned with business needs.

  • Device management: Help lead the rollout and ongoing development of JumpCloud and our device management practices across macOS, Windows, and Linux. Define and implement device configurations, security policies, software deployment, and onboarding processes in partnership with IT Operations and Security.

  • Automation and employee lifecycle: Design and improve onboarding, role changes, and offboarding across identity, devices, and SaaS tools. Use tools such as Okta Workflows, n8n, Python, and APIs to reduce manual work and make processes more reliable.

  • Continuous improvement: Assess our current systems, identify gaps, and turn findings into practical improvements. Investigate complex issues across connected services, address root causes, and follow through until changes are working well.

  • SaaS administration and governance: Administer our core internal tools and help evaluate new applications. Establish clear practices for application setup, integrations, access requests, approvals, and access reviews.

  • Security and compliance: Partner with Security and the Risk and Audit team to implement and maintain controls across identity, Google Workspace, devices, and SaaS tools. Automate evidence collection where practical to support ISO 27001 and SOC 2 Type 2.

  • Project delivery and mentoring: Lead projects from scoping and technical design through rollout and handover. Coordinate dependencies, communicate risks and progress, and help colleagues grow through documentation, reviews, and knowledge sharing.

What you bring

  • Broad IT engineering experience: You have hands-on experience across identity, collaboration tools, endpoint management, and SaaS administration. You understand how these systems connect and can troubleshoot problems across them.

  • Depth in a core area: You bring strong expertise in at least one of Okta, Google Workspace, or JumpCloud, along with the ability to work across the others. We welcome different strengths; you do not need to be equally expert in all three.

  • Device management deployment: You have helped deploy or significantly improve an MDM or endpoint management platform. You can turn security and operational requirements into workable configurations, test them, and roll them out with minimal disruption.

  • Automation and scripting: You build reliable automation using workflow tools, APIs, webhooks, and Python or a comparable scripting language. You consider error handling, monitoring, and ongoing maintenance.

  • A track record of improvement: You can share examples of systems or processes you assessed, improved, and delivered, with clear results for employees or the IT team.

  • Proactive judgment and ownership: You work independently, make sound technical decisions, and know when to involve others. You can turn an unclear problem into a practical plan, explain trade-offs, and take responsibility for the outcome.

  • Security and compliance awareness: You have implemented controls such as access reviews, secure configurations, or device policies, and understand how to document and demonstrate that they work. Experience supporting ISO 27001 or SOC 2 is valuable.

  • Clear communication and collaboration: You work effectively in a fully remote team and communicate clearly with technical and non-technical colleagues across cultures. You share knowledge and help others become more effective.

  • Experience: Typically six or more years in IT engineering, systems administration, identity, or endpoint management, with increasing responsibility for technical decisions and project delivery. Equivalent experience matters more than a specific number of years.

Bonus points

  • Experience supporting mergers and acquisitions, including assessing and integrating identity systems, Google Workspace environments, devices, or SaaS tools.

  • Experience in a developer-heavy or engineering-led company.

  • Experience supporting both ISO 27001 and SOC 2 Type 2, including automated evidence collection.

  • Professional proficiency in French.

Where we hire

At Upsun, remote work isn’t just a trend. It’s our foundation. Upsunners are a global workforce, and we thrive in a multicultural team. We’re committed to open source and an open, welcoming environment. Our team spans more than 30 countries and a wide range of experience levels, and we’re currently hiring for this role in Canada. We’re unable to provide visa sponsorship at this time, but we welcome applications from all qualified candidates who are legally authorized to work in these countries.

How we hire

Our interview process is a chance for us to understand how you think, what you’ve built, and what you want to take on next, and for you to get to know us. Together, we’ll explore where your strengths and interests meet the challenges our teams are solving.

We know a great hire won’t meet every requirement above. If you can see yourself making the team better, we want to hear your story. Few of us would be here if someone hadn’t taken a chance on us.

  4. 45 Minutes with Executive (Senior Director, FP&A & IT)

A global team - Collaborate with colleagues from diverse backgrounds across the world, embracing different perspectives

Benefits and perks - Make the most of what matters to you

Flexible PTO

Comprehensive healthcare coverage (UK, Canada, France, Spain)

Company stock options

Professional development budget

Office equipment budget

Annual team gatherings

Inclusive parental leave

You belong here

title: MSP Mac Help Desk Guru (work from home)
description: Headquarters: ignitionit.com URL: https://ignitionit.com Fully Remote · Work from home · Full-time (Eastern or Pacific time zones) · Apple-first TL;DR ignitionit.com is a seasoned, Apple-first MSP — in business for almost 30 years — and we're hiring a Help Desk Technician to be the friendly, capable first voice our clients reach when something isn't working. This position is a remote, work-from-home, full-time role. We've written this as a junior-to-mid-level job description because that's where most great people start on our team. But if you're more seasoned — comfortable in identity, MDM, or security work — don't scroll past. We'd be delighted to find someone who can step in higher up the ladder, and we'll happily talk about a more senior scope and comp if that's you. What the actual job??? Unlike many IT shops, we believe that the technology is the tactic. The actual job is making people feel taken care of. One of our core values is “49% tech support, 51% human support.” You'll succeed by configuring devices, resetting access, untangling email, and chasing down the gremlin that's been haunting someone's conference room. But you'll know you succeeded when a client exhales and says, “Thank goodness you're on it!” That Warm Fuzzy Feeling™ is the actual product. The green lights on the dashboard are just how we get there. In a typical week, you might: Onboard a new hire at a fast-growing startup: provision their Mac, set up their Google Workspace or Microsoft 365 accounts, enroll the device in MDM, and make sure day one feels effortless. Offboard a departing employee cleanly — recover the laptop, revoke access, and close the loop so nothing's left dangling. All boxes checked, ticket notated and closed, client followed up with. Field a "my email stopped working" ticket that turns out to be a DNS thing, a phishing-filter thing, or a "they changed their password on their phone three weeks ago" thing. Help a family office or RIA get a touchy Zoom Room or conference-room AV setup behaving before a meeting — over the phone. Triage the queue so phones get answered fast, emails don't rot, and nobody feels forgotten — even when the honest answer is, “We're on it, but here's the realistic timeline." ⠀ You'll be the front line: helping with what you can, researching what you can't, and pinging the rest of the team when you're genuinely stuck. That last part is a skill, not a weakness — knowing when to ask is half the job. About ignitionit.com We're one of the oldest Apple Technical Partners on the planet, and one of the only certified Apple Premier Partners — that’s kinda like getting knighted by the ghost of Steve Jobs. We started where you’d expect to find Macs (creative agencies, non-profits, education) but our primary clients today are cutting-edge, venture-backed AI SaaS startups, VC and private equity firms, registered investment advisors — many of them operating under stringent compliance expectations (SOC 2, SEC). That means we hold ourselves to a higher standard than the scrappy shop we started as. Polished, reliable, security-minded work is the baseline now — but always with a smile! What hasn't changed: relationships are still our most valuable currency — with clients, with vendors, and with each other. We're a tight, supportive team. We teach each other what we know, cover for each other when life throws a punch, and care a little too much about doing things the right way. We're still a bit weird, and our clients seem to like us that way. We move fast, priorities shift, it’s not always documented (whatever it is), our tool set and list of supported platforms is sprawling, and some days the to-do list is longer than you'd like. If you can stay warm under pressure, create order out of chaos, learn new stuff fast because you love it, and speak up when you need help, you'll thrive here. If you need a rigid, fully-documented, never-changes environment where nobody trusts you with admin access, where you will be micro-managed so you never have to wonder whether or not you’re doing the right thing, this isn't it. You’ll have a ton of independence on our team, and freedom to use your best judgment to get the ball over the finish line, but that also means we expect you to be naturally responsible, honest, and highly accountable — to yourself, your teammates, and the clients. As they say, the price of freedom is eternal vigilance. The tech you'll work with (and grow into) Day one, you'll be living in: Apple at the core — macOS, iOS, Apple Business Manager, and MDM (Jamf / Iru / Intune / Workspace ONE / and more) Yes, PCs too — about one-third of our users are driving Windows Google Workspace and Microsoft 365 admin consoles Identity and access — SSO, MFA, and security keys (Okta, Entra ID, Yubikey, and friends) Lots of other security tools — our stack is constantly evolving and may vary from client to client The everyday productivity stack — Slack, Zoom, conference-room AV, networking basics (Meraki), and endpoint tooling ⠀ You don't need to know all of this. You need to be the kind of person who wants to. As you grow, there's a clear path into infrastructure administration, project architecture and implementation, and — for the right person — security and compliance work (phishing simulations, endpoint detection, SOC 2 / CIS / SEC readiness, due diligence questionnaire support, etc.). That's where our most senior people live, and it's wide open. Who we hope you are The hard requirements — we won't move forward unless you: Can work standard business hours in Eastern or Pacific time zones (we currently need both) Have a quiet home workspace and reliable broadband Have proven Apple aptitude — you actually use and like the Apple ecosystem Have at least 5 years of IT support experience on the job. ⠀ Everything else — and this is the longer list, on purpose. We figure technical skills are teachable; character takes a lot longer. So we're looking for someone who: Genuinely cares — about clients, teammates, and doing right by people Loves to learn, and proves it in how they spend their time Reads, and writes clearly — clear writing is clear thinking, and you'll do a lot of it Stays calm and kind with a frustrated person on the other end of the line Can tell the difference between good customer service and fantastic customer service, and refuses to settle for the former Notices when something's being done inefficiently and fixes it (you may boast about it later, that’s fine) Proofreads their own work (yes, we noticed whether you proofread your application) Has a sense of humor, and doesn't take themselves too seriously Regarding AI Our company founder/CEO is headquartered in the Bay Area. We work with innovative, ambitious companies developing AI products. Our team members hold a range of opinions about whether AI is “good or bad” for humans, but at the end of the day, we embrace the plain fact that it is here, we must embrace it to evolve, and our clients increasingly depend on us to help them embrace it, too, to help them evolve and stay competitive. Our CEO's opinion: AI will not replace human labor any time soon; rather, AI is a new opportunity to either (a) get things done faster, or (b) get a much higher quality of output than before. If you’re an AI tinkerer, great! We want to hear how you’re using it and see your latest vibe project. If you’re allergic to AI or have no interest in learning new habits to work effectively with it, this is not the place for you. Compensation & logistics Base salary: Applicants outside the USA will be compensated according to your local employment market. For applicants closer to the junior side who are located in the USA, $50,000–$65,000/yr, depending on experience level and your local geographical price index. With experience, comp goes up from there. Genuinely experienced, more senior candidates can be slotted higher — let's talk. Type & location: Full-time, work from home, fully remote. Eastern or Pacific time zones. Benefits: Medical / dental / vision for the employee, 401(k) with employer contribution, 2 weeks of PTO annually to start, and a stipend for your home internet. How to apply The first step is really easy and only takes 10 minutes — no resume, no cover letter, no essays. Here's how: Take this online Culture Index assessment (about 10 minutes): We use it to screen for people whose natural wiring fits how our team works. If your profile lines up with what we're looking for, we'll reach out and ask you to complete a 60-minute TestGorilla assessment for critical thinking skills, send us your resume, and maybe a couple of other items. From there, we conduct between 2-4 video interviews. One of these might be a live technical assessment. If the Culture Index step feels like a strange way to start a job application — that's kind of the point. Remember the phrase Think Different? Ignition is an equal opportunity employer. We welcome and will consider all qualified applicants. Good luck in your search — and may the Force be with you! To apply: https://weworkremotely.com/remote-jobs/ignition-inc-msp-mac-help-desk-guru-work-from-home

Our CEO's opinion: AI will not replace human labor any time soon; rather, AI is a new opportunity to either (a) get things done faster, or (b) get a much higher quality of output than before. If you’re an AI tinkerer, great! We want to hear how you’re using it and see your latest vibe project. If you’re allergic to AI or have no interest in learning new habits to work effectively with it, this is not the place for you.

Compensation & logistics

  • Base salary: Applicants outside the USA will be compensated according to your local employment market. For applicants closer to the junior side who are located in the USA, $50,000–$65,000/yr, depending on experience level and your local geographical price index. With experience, comp goes up from there. Genuinely experienced, more senior candidates can be slotted higher — let's talk. 

  • Type & location: Full-time, work from home, fully remote. Eastern or Pacific time zones.

  • Benefits: Medical / dental / vision for the employee, 401(k) with employer contribution, 2 weeks of PTO annually to start, and a stipend for your home internet.

How to apply

The first step is really easy and only takes 10 minutes — no resume, no cover letter, no essays. Here's how:

  1. Take this online Culture Index assessment (about 10 minutes): We use it to screen for people whose natural wiring fits how our team works.

  2. If your profile lines up with what we're looking for, we'll reach out and ask you to complete a 60-minute TestGorilla assessment for critical thinking skills, send us your resume, and maybe a couple of other items.

  3. From there, we conduct between 2-4 video interviews. One of these might be a live technical assessment.

If the Culture Index step feels like a strange way to start a job application — that's kind of the point. Remember the phrase Think Different?

Ignition is an equal opportunity employer. We welcome and will consider all qualified applicants. Good luck in your search — and may the Force be with you!

raw.title: Ping Identity: Director, Global Alliances – Accenture
raw.description:
Headquarters: USA - Remote

About Ping Identity: 

At Ping Identity, we believe in making digital experiences both secure and seamless for all users, without compromise. We call this digital freedom. And it's not just something we provide our customers. It's something that inspires our company. People don't come here to join a culture that's built on digital freedom. They come to cultivate it. 

Our intelligent, cloud identity platform lets people shop, work, bank, and interact wherever and however they want. Without friction. Without fear. 

While protecting digital identities is at the core of our technology, protecting individual identities is at the core of our culture. We champion every identity. One of our core values, Respect Individuality, reminds us to celebrate differences so you are empowered to bring your authentic self to work. 

We're headquartered in Denver, Colorado and we have offices and employees around the globe. We serve the largest, most demanding enterprises worldwide, including more than half of the Fortune 100. At Ping Identity, we're changing the way people and businesses think about cybersecurity, digital experiences, and identity and access management. 

Ping Identity is seeking a strategic, commercially minded, and highly influential Director, Global Alliances – Accenture to own and accelerate our relationship with Accenture worldwide.

This is a high-impact global leadership role—not a regional partner-management position. You will serve as Ping’s single accountable alliance leader for Accenture, shaping the global strategy, executive relationship, operating model, and joint go-to-market plan across Accenture’s Identity, Security, Technology, Song, industry, cloud, delivery, and managed-services organizations.

The successful candidate will turn a complex global relationship into a focused, repeatable growth engine—aligning executives, mobilizing Ping’s teams, and helping Accenture make Ping the identity platform of choice in strategic transformation programs.

This is a hands-on builder role. You will craft the strategy, create the operating model, and drive execution from executive alignment through customer outcomes. You will build top-down and bottoms-up engagement and convert shared priorities into strategic collaboration agreements, joint investment plans, and measurable results.

What you will own

Global alliance strategy and executive leadership

  • Define and execute a multi-year global Accenture alliance strategy aligned to Ping’s corporate priorities, growth objectives, product strategy, and regional plans.
  • Establish trusted relationships with Accenture’s global and regional executives across Identity, Cybersecurity, Technology, Song, cloud, industry, delivery, and managed services.
  • Act as Ping’s primary global Accenture leadership point and orchestrate executive alignment when priorities, resources, commercial interests, or customer pursuits require senior intervention.
  • Build and maintain a joint annual business plan with clear priorities, investments, owners, milestones, and measurable outcomes.
  • Create a global-to-local operating model that gives AMER, EMEA, and APJ teams a common strategy while allowing appropriate regional and country-level activation.
  • Drive GTM Acceleration, ensuring Ping is front-and-center with Accenture SAL’s and CAL’s across industry verticals.  

Strategic engagement and collaboration agreements

  • Build a deliberate, multi-threaded engagement model with Accenture’s global leadership, practice executives, industry leaders, regional sponsors, account executives, and delivery leaders.
  • Create executive alignment around a small number of strategic priorities, including the business case, mutual value, investment requirements, customer outcomes, and path to scale.
  • Develop, advance, and operationalize strategic collaboration agreements, memoranda of understanding, annual business plans, and related partnership frameworks with Accenture.
  • Translate agreements into clear gives-and-gets, governance structures, named owners, investment principles, milestones, escalation paths, and measurable success criteria.
  • Partner with Ping Finance, Legal, Operations, Product, Sales, Sales Engineering, Professional Services, and executive leadership to ensure agreements are commercially sound, executable, and connected to Ping’s broader strategy.
  • Establish a cadence of executive briefings, steering committees, business reviews, and working sessions that keeps both organizations aligned and accountable.
  • Identify when a relationship should progress from informal collaboration to a formal strategic agreement, and lead the internal and partner process required to make that progression successful.

Joint go-to-market and revenue growth

  • Develop a disciplined joint go-to-market motion spanning “to,” “with,” and “through” Accenture partner routes.
  • Build and manage a prioritized target-account strategy, including account mapping, install-base intelligence, whitespace analysis, opportunity hypotheses, and executive sponsorship.
  • Mobilize Ping account teams and Accenture sales, account, industry, and practice leaders around qualified opportunities and strategic pursuits.
  • Drive partner-sourced, partner-influenced, co-sell, resale, services-attach, and expansion revenue while establishing clear definitions for attribution and credit.
  • Create repeatable joint offers and sales plays that connect Ping’s identity security platform with Accenture’s consulting, implementation, transformation, and managed-services capabilities.
  • Improve pipeline quality, progression, forecast accuracy, win rates, deal velocity, and strategic account penetration through consistent inspection and action planning.
  • Ensure that the partnership produces referenceable customer outcomes—not only activity, meetings, or enablement attendance.

Governance, operating rhythm, and accountability

  • Establish a practical governance model with executive sponsorship, a named steering committee, working teams, escalation paths, and clear decision rights.
  • Lead monthly operating reviews, quarterly business reviews, and annual planning sessions with Ping and Accenture executives.
  • Maintain a shared scorecard covering pipeline, bookings, revenue, services attach, target-account engagement, enablement, certifications, delivery capacity, joint offers, lighthouse customers, customer outcomes, and referenceability.
  • Convert strategic intent into 30-, 60-, and 90-day execution plans with named owners and measurable milestones.
  • Identify execution gaps early, make trade-offs explicit, and hold both organizations accountable for commitments.
  • Partner with Finance, Legal, Operations, and leadership teams to establish sound commercial, investment, compliance, and reporting practices.

Enablement, delivery, and customer success

  • Work with the partner enablement team to build a scalable enablement strategy for Accenture sales, solution architects, consultants, and delivery professionals.
  • Align Ping Professional Services, Customer Success, Sales Engineering, Product, Support, Enablement and other partner delivery resources to improve implementation quality, customer outcomes, and feedback loops.
  • Connect enablement to pipeline, pursuits, implementations, services attach, and customer outcomes.
  • Set targets, identify gaps, coordinate Ping resources, and report progress through alliance governance and quarterly business reviews.

Cross-functional leadership inside Ping

  • Serve as Accenture’s connective tissue between Global Alliances and Sales, Sales Engineering, Product, Product Marketing, Partner Marketing, Professional Services, Customer Success, Finance, Legal, and Operations.
  • Create clarity on roles, resources, pursuit strategy, deal engagement, channel conflict, commercial guardrails, and escalation paths.
  • Champion partner-led execution across Ping’s global field organization and make it easy for sellers to understand when and how to engage Accenture.
  • Represent the voice of Accenture internally while protecting Ping’s strategic, customer, commercial, and operational interests.
  • Build a culture of ownership, transparency, urgency, and measurable execution across the virtual alliance team.

What success looks like

Success will be measured by:

  • An adopted global strategy, strong executive relationships, and effective governance.
  • Strategic collaboration agreements with clear mutual commitments, investments, and outcomes.
  • Growth in qualified pipeline, bookings, revenue, and services attach for both Ping and Accenture.
  • A measurable Accenture enablement and delivery capability, supported by training, certifications, and capacity.
  • Stronger field execution, forecast discipline, new logos, renewals and referenceable outcomes.

What you bring

  • Experience building and managing strategic relationships with Accenture, ideally across global or regional practices.
  • Experience in cybersecurity; experience with identity is a strong plus.
  • Experience building and scaling programs—from strategy and operating model through enablement, execution, and measurement.
  • International experience working across regions, cultures, and complex global organizations.
  • 12+ years of experience in channels, sales, or related fields

Base Hiring Range: $200,000-$215,000 + variable commission

Most importantly, we keep hiring talented, smart, fun, and genuinely nice people because that’s who we want to succeed with every day.

Consequential Work. Dedicated People.


About Onebrief

Onebrief builds collaboration and AI-powered workflow software for military planning and operational coordination.

Military planning is complex by nature, requiring teams to coordinate information, people, and decisions across systems and locations. Onebrief brings planning, collaboration, simulation, and AI into one connected environment, helping teams test strategies, adapt to changing conditions, and make decisions with greater clarity when the stakes are real.

We are a distributed team of builders from military, operational, and technology backgrounds who care deeply about improving how important work gets done. Some team members work remotely, while others work directly alongside customers in operational environments around the world.

Founded in 2019, Onebrief is backed by leading investors including General Catalyst, Battery Ventures, Insight Partners, Sapphire Ventures, and Human Capital. Valued at more than $2 billion, we continue to invest in product innovation, AI capabilities, and team growth.

Why This Role Exists

As a Solutions Engineer at Onebrief, you work where mission, engineering, and compliance meet.

You'll own technical solution design and deployment readiness, translating customer requirements into secure, scalable deployment architectures. You'll partner with Platform Engineering, SRE, and our Cybersecurity team to validate infrastructure, configure environments, resolve technical blockers, and successfully transition solutions into production.

Youâll work with our go-to-market and customer facing teams to meet with planners, operations officers, and network owners to understand how they work today. Youâll help show them what that work looks like in Onebrief, and then you'll make it real.

You connect a staff's planning problem to a live, accredited Onebrief deployment.

What You'll Do

Core responsibilities:

  • Run technical discovery. With Sales and Engineering, map a staff's current workflow and pain points, specifically focusing on their technical constraints: networks, hosting, identity, and integration requirements, especially in multi-network environments.

  • Lead deployment engineering. Coordinate the technical delivery of new deployments, including infrastructure validation, network configuration checks, and system readiness verification. Write code to configure new deployments and support new environments.

  • Support accreditation. Help create and review security documentation, including STIG checklists and ATO artifacts, alongside our cybersecurity team so deployments are accredited on the customer's timeline.

  • Align stakeholders. Get technical stakeholders on both sides to agree on requirements, constraints, and tradeoffs, so customers see value sooner. Ensure those technical requirements are properly translated into contract deliverables.

  • Scope integrations. Design how Onebrief Connect fits into a command's ecosystem: APIs, data pipelines, Foundry and Maven Smart System, CUOPS tools, and dashboards.

  • Deliver tailored demos. Lead technical demonstrations and solution validation, partnering with Sales and customer-facing teams to demonstrate Onebrief's technical capabilities, deployment architecture, security posture, and integration options.

raw.title: Discord: Engineering Manager, Platform Security
raw.description:
Headquarters: Remote (West Coast)

Discord has a highly engaged community of millions of daily active users who use the platform for many different reasons, but there’s one thing that nearly everyone does: play video games. Discord plays a uniquely important role in the future of gaming, and we are focused on making it easier and more fun for people to hang out before, during, and after playing games.

More broadly, Discord is about empowering people to find belonging in all kinds of communities, and those people trust us to keep their communications safe. Our Platform Security Engineering team protects the systems we use to create Discord, making the “secure way” the “easy way.”

We’re looking for an Engineering Manager to lead a team of software engineers in articulating and pursuing the most leveraged opportunities to reduce security risk across Engineering. This team will design and build lovable “paved paths” for managing identities and access, shipping code, configuring cloud infrastructure, and operating services. If you’re an Engineering Manager who’s deeply curious, eager to own technically and socially complex projects, and excited to improve security and privacy at Discord, read on!

 

What you'll do

You’ll shape company-wide security strategy and lead a highly-autonomous and horizontally-integrated team of software engineers who will...

  • Develop and apply best-in-class secure baselines for cloud infrastructure, owning the security of all cloud environments
  • Manage infrastructure vulnerabilities while supporting a high-velocity engineering org with hundreds of developers
  • Secure first- and third-party software supply chains, from the dev environment through CI/CD and into production
  • Build and operate identity and access management (IAM) systems for humans and machines that are user-friendly and promote least privilege
  • Consult on risk assessments, architectural designs, threat models, code reviews, and more—pragmatically balancing security with other business considerations

What we look for

  • 3+ years of experience as people manager, having managed a team of 3+ security software engineers
  • Passion for creating diverse and inclusive teams and coaching engineers
  • 3+ years of experience securing systems with millions of users
  • Comfort with writing the roadmap, not just following one
  • Experience building in and securing cloud-based environments (we use GCP, Cloudflare, and AWS)
  • Expert reasoning about the security of complex systems, even if they contain unfamiliar components
  • Experience writing software in a general-purpose programming language (we use Python, Typescript, and Rust)
  • Experience developing with agentic AI, and a good grasp of AI security practices

Bonus points if you have…

  • Understanding of modern authentication and authorization concepts (e.g. RBAC, OAuth, Zero Trust network architectures, mTLS)
  • Familiarity with build and CI/CD technologies (e.g. Terraform, Bazel, Buildkite, Spacelift)
  • Experience defining and orchestrating containers (e.g. via Kubernetes, Docker, Distroless, OCI) and serverless workloads (e.g. Cloudflare Workers)
  • Experience with running and operationalizing security platforms such as Wiz

 

This position is West Coast (U.S.) based and can be remote but if you live in the Bay Area, you’re welcome to work from our beautiful SF office.

The base salary range for this full-time position is listed below. This position will also be eligible for equity and benefits. Our salary ranges are determined by role and level. Within the range, individual pay is determined by additional factors, including job-related skills, experience, and relevant education or training. Please note that the compensation details listed in role postings reflect the base salary only, and do not include equity, or benefits.

$248,000—$310,000 USD

Discord plays a uniquely important role in the future of gaming. We're a multiplatform, multigenerational and multiplayer platform that helps people deepen their friendships around games and shared interests, and helps developers build and grow their businesses. We believe games give us a way to have fun with our favorite people, whether listening to music together or grinding in competitive matches for diamond rank. Join us in our mission! This team has a track record of exceeding targets, and your role will help them to work with partners to drive a repeatable, scalable sales motion. You will spend meaningful time in the field with partner and Ping sales teams, building rep-to-rep engagement and turning joint account plans into qualified pipeline and closed business. You will also help organize regional partner engagements that bring the right teams together around target accounts and repeatable go-to-market plays. This is a builder role for someone who is thoughtful, positive, curious, and ready to turn strategy into action. Drive rep-to-rep engagement between Ping sellers and partner sellers, helping teams identify opportunities, coordinate pursuits, and progress new-logo deals. Set up and support regional partner events, including field meetings, account-mapping sessions, enablements, workshops, roundtables, and other activities designed to create partner-to-partner engagement and qualified pipeline. Develop repeatable partner go-to-market plays and practical enablement that help partners position Ping Identity, engage new enterprise accounts, and progress opportunities. Partner with Enterprise sales, Partner Solutions Engineering, marketing, services, and product teams to remove friction and help partners win and deliver successfully. Track partner activity, event engagement, sourced and influenced pipeline, new-logo progress, and follow-through; use the data to focus time and investment where it will have the greatest impact. Deliver measurable impact by expanding productive partner coverage, increasing partner-led new-logo pipeline, improving rep-to-rep engagement, and turning regional activity into repeatable growth. You Have: 10+ years of experience in channel, alliances, partner sales, or a related go-to-market role in enterprise technology. Experience working with partners to acquire new customers and build sourced or influenced pipeline in the Enterprise market. Experience managing or developing relationships with integrators, resellers, delivery partners, and/or distributors. A track record of building partner programs, joint account plans, field motions, or other repeatable go-to-market plays—not simply managing existing relationships. Strong field presence and the ability to engage credibly with partner executives, sellers, technical teams, and Ping sales leaders. Excellent communication and facilitation skills, including the ability to create productive rep-to-rep conversations and turn meetings into clear next steps. A positive, practical, and collaborative approach; you create momentum, follow through on commitments, and are comfortable operating in a changing environment. Willingness to travel regularly and spend meaningful time with partners, customers, and internal teams in the field. Bonus Points If You Have: Experience in cybersecurity, identity and access management, or another complex enterprise technology category. Experience working with both national and regional partners, or building partner coverage in new territories. Experience planning and executing regional partner events, roundtables, workshops, or field marketing programs. Experience creating partner enablement programs, certifications, technical workshops, or sales plays. Experience working with sales development, account executives, and partner sellers to create net-new opportunities. Enthusiasm for representing the company at partner forums, industry events, roundtables, and other public-facing engagements. A relevant degree or equivalent experience, and/or cybersecurity or channel-related certifications. Salary Range: $88,000–$132,000 base + Commission In accordance with Colorado’s Equal Pay for Equal Work Act (SB 19-085) the approximate compensation range for this role in Colorado is listed above. Life at Ping: We believe in and facilitate a flexible, collaborative work environment. We’re growing quickly, but remain true to the innovative, can-do startup values that got us here. Most importantly, we keep hiring talented, smart, fun, and genuinely nice people because that’s who we want to succeed with every day. Here are just a few of the things that make Ping special: A company culture that empowers you to do your best work. Employee Resource Groups that create a sense of belonging for everyone. Regular company and team bonding events. Competitive benefits and perks. Global volunteering and community initiatives Our Benefits: Generous PTO & Holiday Schedule Parental Leave Progressive Healthcare Options Retirement Programs Opportunity for Education Reimbursement Commuter Offset (Specific locations) Ping is the collective sum of all our individual experiences, backgrounds and influences and we pride ourselves in growing and learning together.
